After much deliberation, I have decided to endorse this application, but not without serious criticism.
Before I begin my review, for context, I just want to provide a little background so that you understand how difficult it is to use the Deep Fritz 14 software.
I am a chess club / tournament player.  I have been playing and studying chess for ~15 years.
I have had an account on
now for roughly 6 years.
My Rapid rating on
is 1378
My Daily rating on
is 1429
I am also a PC Support Analyst that is responsible for supporting nearly 60 software applications.
Prior to owning Fritz 14, I have owned every single copy of the Chessmaster series, going all the way back to Chessmaster 4000.
I wanted to move on to a more 'serious' chess application, to be where the professionals do their work and analysis.
PROS:
- Deep Fritz 14 seems to be stable under Windows 10 and doesn't crash.   Unlike Chessmaster XI  / grandmaster edition.
- Deep Fritz 14 supports multiple CPU engine options.  Fantastic if you're like me and have built a nice quad-core gaming PC with 8 threads.  You can turn on the 8 CPU feature.
- Deep Fritz 14 has a rich Database selection, creation and editor.
- The 3D board rotation tool is nicely done.
CONS:
-  First time users of Fritz will be completely LOST.  Good luck, mate!
- The GUI feels old, similar to the GIMP 2 art program.   Very clunky.
- The Help Menu in Deep Fritz 14 does not contain things like "Search Documentation" or "About Fritz 14" or "Check for Updates".    You know, the kinds of things you would see in ANY other windows application.    But Ohhhh Noooo,  Deep Fritz 14 is special, it gives you two useless options:  They are    1. Send a Smile, or 2. Send a Frown.    What the heck is this garbage?   I thought Deep Fritz 14 was supposed to be a serious chess application?
- Oh, I found the Help, it is a tiny link in the top right corner of the window.  So there are TWO Helps in the same application window?  Not a good look for the developer.

- The 3D boards are too dark.  Yuck.   Why can't I choose a different background color behind the 3D boards?   Why is the background always black?
- There should be more 2D Board Styles and Piece Styles for the money you pay.  Not a good look for the developer.
- The " Table " Button should be renamed to " 2D Background "  because that's what it does.   If you are using a 3D Board, and you click Table, it toggles you back into 2D view and changes the background.

- How is it helpful to show the duplicate text "DGT Board" under the DGT Board option if all the tool tip tells you is that it Activates the DGT board ?   LOL.

- None of the buttons in the dockable windows provide a tool-tip when you hover the mouse cursor over them.
- Why does the LiveBook Tab have a Green LED and a Disconnect Button, but when you hover the mouse cursor over them, there are no Tool-Tips?    This is not good if we have to dig into the user guide to have some sense as to what these are used for.
- In the Engine Window, why is there another Green LED ( Oh no! More Lights )  saying that I am connected to
when I do not have an account and never connect to the site?   This makes no sense.   And why am I given the option to "Disconnect" when I never told it to connect in the first place?
- There are superfluous features in Deep Fritz 14 that many serious chess players would never even think of using, but the developer seems to force them into the GUI without providing an intuitive way to select more simple GUI setups.    Yet simple things like Radio Buttons inside the Move List window get overlooked?
- What is cloud?  What do I need Cloud for?   Unfortunately, I'll never know because there is no Tool-Tip that pops up when I hover the mouse cursor over it !!!!
- There are no radio buttons inside the Move List window like there is for Chessmaster and every other friggin chess application out there in existence.   I guess because Deep Fritz 14 is for the  'serious' chess player,  the developer felt that the GUI window needed to be "harder to use?" Huh?" to make you understand why you spent so much money?
- It is very easy to accidentally "mess up" your "view" inside of Fritz, and if you don't know how to fix it, it is easier to just close out and re-launch the application!   Again, this is not a good look for the developer.   I am not stupid, I support windows applications for a living, this application needs to be completely re-tooled.
-  Similarly, it is very easy to "get lost" inside of the Deep Fritz 14 Menu system and click the wrong thing and go somewhere you didn't intend.    And when it happens, it's easier to just close out of the applciation and re-launch the entire thing.
-The GUI is nearly Impossible to master simply by intuition and 'playing around'.
-You can't just click File > Open > and import a PGN file into Fritz, yeah I know, that seems to be asking too much!
* You are expected to actually to open the PGN file in Windows Notepad, then copy the text into windows clipboard, and finally select "Paste Game" from the Home Tab on the Ribbon.
-You have to watch Youtube Videos to figure out how to get Fritz to do the things you want it to do.
-  It's been two years now, and I still haven't figured out how after importing a PGN game, to make Deep Fritz play as my opponent and have me play as the 'human' player so that I can simply 'test possible moves' for the current position.  Fritz makes things more difficult than they  need to be.  This should be an easy thing to do.  I know this is possible, and seems to be the most important need for club players but I can't find any youtube videos on how to do this.   FRITZ makes me want to walk away for two weeks before I come back and try again.

This game has been a long time favorite, and is a great addition for anyone who enjoys the tower defense genre of gaming. The levels are simple in design, yet force you to think of how you want to lay out your design carefully. Some levels push this a bit farther, giving you multiple ways to maze and build. This really comes into focus during the later maps of the Story Mode, where the enemies have literally a dozen pathing options.
On top of the typical story mode there are also many different challenge modes for each map, giving hours of enjoyment. Modes include: Grinder and Super Grinder, 99 waves that get progressively harder as you go; Green Towers Only, where you can't upgrade your towers at all; Story Reversed, that swaps the direction the enemies travel; and much more.
There are also a few extra campaigns available through DLC, as well as community driven content with tons of maps to try out. All in all, it's a very solid pickup for any of you Tower Defense fans out there, and an enjoyable game all around.

Warhammer 40K: Armaggeddon is a hex based game and is worth all the money that you'll be dishing out. The story is about the 1st invasion of Hive World of Armaggeddon. Which in case you don't know is a planet of huge mega city towers with everything wrong with china on steroids. In this polluted, firey wasteland; you are forced to repel and protect the planet from gajillions of Orks and DA BIGGEST BADDEST WARLORD AROUND Margaret Thatcher.
The story is rather competent and is brought to life by the amazing cast of voice actors and art. The main story is divided into three acts, each of them all very meaty. If you manage to snatch this game on sale, I'll guarantee that you won't be testing out that refund button anytime soon.
I always found hex-based strategy games to be rather tedious due to how much number crunching you had to do but I have to say that the UI of Armageddon is the strongest part of the game. You can check what each stats do by clicking the stats and with the ability to compare units, I have to say I actually found out that I kinda knew what I was doing (A rare occurence I must admit).
There are so many different units in the game, all so full of flavor and tasty fluff. Commanders waving power swords, walking gun fortresses, and midget snipers. Combined with decent animations and sound effects I felt like I had a proper commander of the Steel Legion.
Now to summarise, despite my glowing review I did get overwhelmed by the sheer variety of options but take it slowly and check out different options and button. Experimentation is key. You'll notice that as the ball starts to get rolling, that it'll get harder to stop.

I've been playing 40k video games since the days of SSi's Chaos Gate and Rites of War. Overall, this is an above average fare of turn based tactics and strategy. The strategic elements are light, and the difficulty isn't too high - any veteran of turn based hex strategy games will be able to breeze though.
6/10 - For those familiar with the 40k universe, this is the 2nd war for armageddon. This game plays it safe and does nothing with the story other than tread through some basic plot points. Nothing to write home about, but the 40k world is rich in details and atmosphere, so it gets a slightly above average score for me.
8/10 - Solid showing of the 40k atmosphere and tone. There is some basic voice acting and still shots between missions with 40k art that feels like a part of the universe. The maps are pleasing to look at for the most part and the unit spirtes look about right. With that said, there was nothing that stuck out to me as being particularly exceptional.
6/10 - This was a rather bog-standard hex based strategy game. The AI seemed rather overly-cautious and at no point did I feel like they were difficult. It is definitely fun moving units around and using superior positioning to destroy your enemies - but there's one major element that works against the game: a turn limit. This force a particularly aggressive mindset of play, and so the game will HEAVYILY favor certain units over others simply due to movemen rates. This feels like weak mechanics to me, as you will find yourself using the same tactics over and over to defeat your opponents. By mission 25, I had basically run an optimial set of units and tactics while the AI struggled to make a dent in my forces.
8/10 - I had a very small handful of crashes during my playthrough. The game can be set up to save before every turn starts however, so no progress is really lost.
4/10 - If I had purchased the vanilla game at full price ($39.99 USD) I would actually feel a bit disappointed. There are other DLC to purchase that will increase playtime - but I haven't tried it yet. Considering that you have to pay for it, that doesn't change my mind one bit regarding the value. I would think that $25 - $30 is a far more fair price for the game that you get.
tl;dr: If you liked SSI's Rites of War, it is basically that game but better. Also, if you like reliving the 2nd War for Armageddon, it does do that. With that said, I'd be hesitent to buy at full price, but it is definitely worth it around the 25-30 dollar mark.

While normal enemies aren't that hard to deal with, you'll encounter some more difficult big enemies here and there, which are still manageable though.
The real issue with this game are the bosses. Since it's 2D, you're limited in your ways of movement, which means that sometimes there is literally no way to dodge some of the boss attacks and some of them can kill you (almost) instantly. + Great graphics
+ Fantastic level design
+ Spectacular and informative sound design
+ Wonderful customization
+ Engaging combat
+ Epic bosses
+ Challenging but fair difficulty
+ Local Co-op
+ New Game Plus option
+/- Lack of Mini Map (Pro for some, con for others)

Okay so first of all, I wanna completely debunk the idea of this being P2W.
This game was never meant as a f2p game. What you are playing when you are f2p, is essentially an infinite trail with restrictions.
Saying that this game is p2w is like saying WoW is p2w.
Because it has an infinite trail with restrictions. It just doesn't make sense.
Now with that out of the way, lets begin with the review.
Mortal Online is a First person, Full loot, Open world and open PvP MMORPG.
Meaning that you can kill anyone, anywhere at anytime.
And when you or someone else dies, thier loot will drop on the ground for anyone to be picked up.
And armor/weapons can not be repaired. Meaning that there will always be room for crafters to supply with more stolen/broken gear.
While the game is still quite buggy as thier development team is rather small.
Most bugs are nowhere near as game breaking as they used to be.
The game has you exploring for countless hours.
Just now i found a certain cave with a monster in it that i have never seen before, after 1600 hours...
There are also alot of dungeons that i know exist but i still haven't been to.
So lack of content is not an issue.
There is one thing though, you can argue that this is a problem or that this completely fixes the game.
There are only 4 character slots per account (They cost 9 euros per slot)
This makes it so that one account can never do all the professions in the game.
This can be really upsetting, but also makes it so that weapons and armor and other crafted items are in more demand as people often have fighters instead of crafters.
The biggest problem i have with the game is that bigger guilds just group up and start killing everybody.
And the only way to not get killed is to join another guild with groups that big. Or be sneaky af ;)
I will continue this review later.

For a game that is all about snipers and sniping, the shooting mechanics are a joke.
You get bullet drop and wind drift all right, but you get a little red circle, that will pop up after an arbitrary amount of time of stearing at an enemy through the scope on medium and easy, that tells you where the shot will go.
On hard you have to guess.
And there lies the problem with the mechanic: When I was taught basic marksmanship, they told me: "don't compensate by eye. Compensate with the adjustable sights."
If the game would have done away with the red circle and instead would have let me adjust for bullet drop and wind drift by hand via those two screws right and on top of the scope, that would have added a whole aditional layer of depth to the game play mechanik. But no.
If the game at least had a descent tutorial where a drill instructor talks you through the basics of shooting, that would have been great. Even if mostly for atmosphere.
Terminal ballistics too seem to have ben programed by someone who never saw a rifle up close.
A 7.62 NATO round can go through two bodys and retain enough power to take out a third? And keeps flying in a perfectly straight line after the second body? Riiiiiight...
But at the same time it wont go through a single layer of brick...
Controlls are in general functional, but as mentioned above, tempramental.

And sometimes even that doesn't work and instead of htting the dirt to avoyd bullets or detection, your character stands up.
Because reasons...
Do I recomend this game?
Well, if you are desperate to kill 5 to 6 hours and have 20 bucks you don't know what else to do with, then go for it.
Otherwise, no.

I have really mixed feelings about this... Especially now, when Ghost Warrior 3 was released.
So let me make it clear; first Ghost Warrior was crappy, unpolished game. It was also ugly, buggy and not enjoyable, maybe excepting headshots... but with buggy animations, as I mentioned before.
Second Ghost Warrior made few things better, but it still has issues. First positive thing is story; of course it is nothing special, but it feels much more grown-up and it's more interesting than in GW 1.
Ending is good. Just good. It's somehow satysfying, but it doesn't drops your jaw.
Second positive thing is improvement of graphics and game engine. The game is running on CryEngine, while first part was built on Chrome Engine 4. Movement is slow, but it makes you feel those heavy "boots" on the ground. Rifle also feels somehow heavy; everything (aiming, taking a shot) takes more time, which makes game more realistic. So making conlusion: gameplay is slower, more realistic and it feels better than in GW 1. Sometimes little glitches appear on killcam, but it doesn't really matters, or does it?
Now let's talk about shooting; as I said before it is slower: it takes time to take down enemy with a good shot. It requies marking enemies with binocular, and using thermal-vision. Than you can take them down one-by one, without alerting anyone. But it's not an open world game, so it is scripted-if you do mission "loud", game will punish you. Enemies with assault rifles can easily detect you, and kill you, so you just MUST do missions stealhly.
Enemy AI is pretty weird-sometimes they don't see you from close range, but sometimes they can spot you from (literally) an end of map. That is just unfinished, and it ruins fun. I think that AI is good, but it is just not really used, so potential is definitly wasted.
Next thing that was "ugh" is number of weapons; while in GW1 you had lot of them, here you are using four sniper rifles and one pistol (which makes five weapons in total, simple maths). No any assault rifles here, which is maybe a good thing, becouse they were in first part, but shooting mechanics were fu***ng broken. So developers just focused on sniper weapons, leaving assault rifles, which is a good thing, becouse we don't have lot of useless stuff.
My conlusion on this game:
Not worth of it's price, but when it is on sale, you can think about buying it.
Especially if you like taking a juicy headshot from 500 meters ;)

This is a great software to run engines in, as well as the three engines included. This is also the only chess software that is available through Steam that takes itself seriously. So you don't have many options anyways. I bought this on Steam sale when it was $19.99 and $9.99 for "64 bit dlc".
You probably would only use the latest Fritz 14 engine, so basically you get one good engine and two old ones. There is a ton of included games from history from all the famous players. They can be searched by all criteria like years, last names, etc. There are many analysis options. You can see suggested moves on the go or analyse the whole game. One nice feature is intentionally vaguely worded hints. They give enough descriptive advice but don't directly give you the best move. You have an option for exact moves though.
While the core of the game is pretty good. But it is really puzzling how a known chess software maker can make a good engine and not take the effort to include more options in its main selling point which is the 2D and 3D representation of the chess board. You get very few options for the 2d chess board. There are nice wooden texture and tones included, but there are just five total! It doesn't even have the green and white traditional vinyl board colors that many players are used to. Doesn't have solid color options. You get too few chess graphics as well, and only 3 out of 5 are any good. The other two are abstract designs no one would use.
The 3d chess board graphics look nice but they look like they've been made very lazily. For example you get a number of options for traditional 3d pieces and boards but they can only be combined with solid color background. You can adjust something as insignificant as lighitng and reflection, but don't get many texture options for the background. The themed 3d graphics with backgrounds are pretty good, but they're mainly for novice players. In my opinion the experienced players would not bother running these nice looking 3d graphics since they are used to plain 2d diagram.
So basically I'd give it a 7 out of 10. You get lots of advanced options but not enough color and graphics variation. I'd even be willing to purchase additional ones as DLC if they were available. But there aren't any. Seems like such a missed opportunity to simply add more colors and graphics options. The only explanation I can think of is lazyness.

I'll try to be as spoiler free as possible, mostly out of respect for the maker and community.
As much as I can see why people are excited for the game I don't enjoy the game myself.
As a puzzle game, most of the puzzles are more or less bring item A to place Y (with a few basic combine item A and B to create item C to bring to place Y and use there). There are a few that stand out which I'll get to later.
The story, while decently written, has a few problems which while not glaring problems can if you notice them make you question how dangerous the situation really is.
While quite a lot of people do mention that they love the characters I can't really agree. For me they feel flat, they have little to tell and they don't do/say enough for you to get to know most of them decently. Which for a game with the user-defnied tag "story-rich" really puts me off, I'm not saying the characters are boring per say just that most you don't get to know past a quick hello and what their occupation is.
As an adventure game the story is fairly short, which doesn't have to be a bad thing. And considering it originated as a flash game this is perfectly understandable. But meanwhile short doesn't mean it has to lack content, which sadly to a somewhat large degree this game does.
The world itself though looks beautiful, and it actually fits the theme of a dying world in need of getting rescued. And the music is in my opinion not bad either, while not memorable it doesn't sound bad during longer stretches of time.
With all this said it probably sounds pretty bad, right? Well it is really not, it is only bad if you're a person like me who focus a lot on smaller "unimportant" details before the larger possibly more important details.
A lot of people enjoy it and I believe it partly is for the few unique puzzles it has.
Quite a few of OneShots puzzles are based around breaking the fourth wall and interacting with the game through the computer, usually requires you to search for a clue in etc. your desktop to get past the puzzle. The execution isn't flawless but at the same time it is very unique and sets it apart from other adventure/puzzle games.
Does this weigh up against the flaws I've found personally? No, but I regress this is a decent game which I do belive has had a bit too much hype regarding the part I believe was the main reason it became popular: It's meta humor.
A lot of games has had it the last few years, but only in smaller degrees usually (with exceptions obviously), and it seems Indie games have picked up on this idea and are actually using it pretty nicely. The thing is, the few clever Meta jokes, observations and puzzles don't really make the overall game better.
All in all, while this game and it's make certainly deserve the attention it gets I'm almost fully certain that if it hadn't been for games like Lisa & Undertale the last few years the idea of a Meta indie game would be much less likely to be successful. So I do believe that this plays a big factor in OneShots popularity, so if you enjoy the game I can see where you're comming from but despite that let me just end this here with this:
I'll say this one final time: It is a decent game that could be worth your money but if you've even the slightest doubt on whatever you'll like it or not then wait on a friend to get it for you or on a sale.
Sadly despite me saying that I can't recommend it in general, but again the game isn't bad just not as great as a lot of people make it out to be.
So if you've read this far thank you for doing so, but if you feel like you don't agree with me then don't and if you feel I was wrong about something major in the review or a bit harsh please mention it as I do appreciate knowing such things and I might rectify such problems.
Minor edit, small clarification: I have to say that the community from what I've seen is good and they don't preach much about the 'greatness' of the game. The community though isn't the game, so while I might be able to say: "You could probably enjoy talking to the community" I can't really say "I recommend the game". The two are different things. So if you only enjoy the story but not the game you'll still probably be able to talk to the community without trouble as of the time of writing this note.

Tower defense at its best. Being able to place your towers in such a way that it forces the baddies to take longer paths is extremely enjoyable and challenging.
Key features:
- Block baddies just as they're getting near your cores, forcing them to re-route.
- Bounce a train of baddies back and forth between two paths by repeatedly opening one and blocking the other.
- Unspent money earns interest so if you build just the towers you need, you'll have even more money later on.
- Create "kill zones" with your most powerful towers + slowing towers + bonus money towers to maximize efficiency.
- Cool story with some great DLC (The Portal cross-over DLC is top notch)
- Alternate modes/achievements will keep you playing for a long time

This is one of several (many?) of the "golf" t ype solitaire games, which are simple, but fun to play. This one is not my favorite--my favorite would be Avalon Legends Solitaire 2--at least I think that's the name. This one is decent though. It adds a couple of twists, including mini-games, which I cheerfully skip, a bonus for playing a card of the same suit as the base card, and certain marked cards that you must be able to play to complete the round successfully. Not quite as interesting to me as the element of resource management and town building that are in Avalon, but others may see it completely differently. It's interesting how all these little twists and elements get added to these solitaire games to differentiate between what is, when you get right down to it, the same game, but the end result is that if you like one of them, you'll probably like them all. So yeah, recommended if you like this type of solitaire.

I was looking forward to Evolve when it first came out, but didn't have time to justify a $60 multiplayer-only shooter. I jumped in as soon as I saw the Free to Play release, played some tutorial to figure it out (the tutorial forces you through Markov's different abilities and lets you see how they work but isn't very useful and it's only for that one hunter but the Goliath monster tutorial seems a bit better but without the story element), and jumped online. I won 4 out of 7 games (played only as hunters) and generally found good teammates. In 2.5 hours I earned about 5k "silver keys" which is about enough to unlock a character (but I put it in upgrades instead).
You set preferences for who you play as and I never played as my bottom two picks (trapper and monster). I only occasionally got my top pick (assault). Changing your preferences is easy.
The store is a mess. You can't sort by price or hunter vs monster for character unlocks. It seems to be a big and unsorted list (two Maggie variants aren't adjacent), but I don't (yet) see a way for them to charge real money. The in-game interface (via character select) works better (aside from the time pressure of the game starting).
I had one game bug out on me where the monster froze in place, the UI displayed paused on the game clock, and the hunters all reported they were stuck. I've had two games where either someone dropped or we failed to get a character (one Caira drop and one Goliath drop). So far, not too bad and the games were still pretty fun.
In the end, it's a fun and unique 4v1 shooter that emphasizes teamwork (hunters) or lone wolf (monster). In my short experience, the play/matchmaking felt balanced enough to provide a constant challenge without being too brutal.
It seems ♥♥♥♥♥♥ what they did to people who originally bought this game (I guess they just got a day's haul in keys), so I'd be wary before dropping money into this game. But for free, it's worth a few hours play time for sure.

I backed this game on Kickstarter when it was announced and I'm definitely glad I did. It's been fun playing through it through the various releases. It was fun to see all the work that goes into polishing up a game for it's finished version.
If you enjoy 2-d platformers and fun & unique games, definitely get it. It takes it roots from old school games like Metal Slug and Contra, but brings its own personality and style to it so that it's not a rip off. It's easy to see where Mercenary King comes from, but it's definitely it's own game. The crafting system is a lot of fun and allows a player to set their own difficulty level by creating weak or strong guns as well as carrying a lot of weight, which will slow down and hinder the player.

While the first words out of most reviewers mouths regarding this game are "metal slug", my impression is that it has taken just as much inspiration from the Megaman games, with a lot of emphasis on careful platforming, learning the patterns of enemies (especially bosses), and choosing the right weapon for the job at hand.
Unlike either Metal Slug or Megaman, you go into each mission with a single gun, knife, and set of passive 'bionic mods', plus whatever limited-use equipment you choose to bring or find mid-mission and passive 'proficiencies' which can be changed at will.  This means planning ahead; while at the home base / lobby you will spend money and materials gained during missions to unlock new gun parts, knives, and mods, and outfit yourself as you like;  Do you set yourself up with an optimal plan for your next mission, or just go with what seems fun? Either way, you have a LOT of options to choose from.
Another unique quality to Mercenary Kings is the large and non-linear qualities of it's maps;  While each of the different levels gets reused for multiple missions, each one is HUGE with numerous interconnected rooms.  Some missions task you with exploring these maps at large on the look-out for specific enemies or materials, while some give you a clearly marked point to reach (or numerous potential boss locations) and you simply need to navigate a favorable route.
Whatever the individual mission objective, it becomes easier and more fun to accomplish with friends.  The co-op REALLY shines when done locally, with two to four friends together in split-screen.  Equally viable is to invite friends online, using steam voice chat or skype for communication.   Public, auto-join online co-op is also available but it's far less ideal, as your only means of communication are a series of quick voice-macros, and there's no way of knowing if the player in charge is thirty missions behind you or thirty missions ahead.   No matter how you choose to do it, the game encourages you to split up and comb different areas of the map, trying to reach or search for your objective, and then meeting up to take on tough bosses together.
Speaking of which, the bosses are another area where the game truly shines.  If you've played earlier in the beta, you'll be amazed at how much improvement was made to the game's varying bosses;  each has a wide variety of different attacks and patterns it will follow and each is equally deadly, enough to challenge the most hardcore action-platformer fan.
In summary, Mercenary Kings draws inspiration from a LOT of things, but it's as new and original as it is nostalgic, and worth checking out.

This game isn't what you think it is.
You probably think it's Metal Slug with customizable guns, which sounds fantastic.  I'd love to play that game.  That's not what this is.  You're not going to run around like a maniac blowing up everything around you.  What you're actually going to do is move carefully forward so you don't get hit, explore every corner of the map over and over, and ultimately get tired and give up.
The main gameplay loop is that you have to move carefully or take damage, which is *very* expensive to repair, and many of the missions involve finding 10 of something on the map...and there's only 10 to find.  And they're not listed on the map.  So you end up exploring the map over and over until you have 9 of 10 collected and you can't find the last one, so you end up going over and over the map, taking damage and dying until eventually you either run out of lives or out of time, and these missions aren't short.  You will put a HUGE ammount of time into these missions and fail them over and over.
Plus you can't alt-tab out of the game, so you can't even look at FAQs or maps to help you.
The game doesn't make you feel strong, it makes you feel like a chump.  The grind takes forever and unless you enjoy finding items scattered and hidden all over the same map over and over, you'll eventually grow to hate it.  I did.  I can't recommend this game.

This is another one of those games, where i am not completely sure what to really think of it. One part of me likes the Artstyle and the gunplay, the other really dislikes the story and the technical stuff.
12 is Better Than 6 gathered my interest because it's a twin stick shooter, and as a big fan of Hotline Miami, i was not only intrigued by the gameplay, but also because of the artstyle.  That you need to reload the guns and, for example, cocking the revolvers i didn't know before going into the game, so it took me a bit by suprise and took a bit of learning until i got completely the hang of it. Mastering it though, feels extremely satisfying, and blasting away a bunch of enemies at once with a few shots is a really cool feeling.
At certain moments in the game, you are also able to purchase different perks by your hard earned (stolen) cash. These perks are pretty usefull, i especially enjoyed the one with the rat and the dynamit, which functions like a homing bomb on enemies.
The gameplay is definitly the stronger point about this game, which kinda makes the lackluster story and the sometimes downright goofy writing worthwhile. I get that it is text only, but i don't see the point of typing out actions of the characters. Or rather, would not like them to talk in an almost roleplaying like way. <he drinks>, <he spits>, <he looks scared>, etc. These are a few examples, which you probably find throughout the entire game. I am really against this sort of narrative, as it ruins not only immersion, but any serious tone to it aswell. I would have much preferred it to let the protagonist explain the actions of characters, or add more sound effects that give off the hints on what the character is doing.
The story itself isn't really all too interesting either. A mexican rambo basically kills everything he doesn't like. I would like to compare this western tale to Red Dead Redemption, but considering that both games are hugely different presentation and budget wise, i think it would be a pretty unfair comparison. Still, i was kind of let down actually to see the game not really going anywhere with its story. Also the ending was downright bad, there is no jumping around here, it's just suddenly over and anti climatic as hell.
My biggest dislike however was this game on a technical level. Random crashes after clearing a mission (in the transission to the next mission it usually happened), enemies often didn't die after getting shot, selecting hats only worked for the certain level then always switched back, enemies downright teleported somewhere else (especially noticable with the guard dogs), got the dialogue skipping achievement for finishing every dialogue normally, some of the speechbubbles of characters you pass by were suddenly in russian, the melee weapons work very strange, and so on. At large times, the game felt really rough around the edges, what made it a bit unpleasent to play through at parts.
But i have to give credit to the very nice soundtrack, which may just contain a few songs and they are repeated throughout the entire game, but they never really get on your nerves and serve the atmosphere well.
Overall, i can recommend this game to everyone who already likes Hotline Miami or twin stick shooters in general, but doesn't expect something of the same caliber as of the former. Everyone else i wouldn't recommend this really as there
first twin stick shooter or even western game at that, there are way better alternatives out there, but as for cheap, i don't think you can make anything really wrong here. It's still fun, even when a bit unpolished.

TL;DR:
Absolute reccomend, but play with a controller if you can.
Yeah, everyone talks about the dedication that went into the art style - and the art is really good!
However, what won the game for me was the gameplay itself. I found myself doing a little fist pump whenever I beat a boss, even if no-one was around to see it. Beating the bosses was so rewarding in itself, because the game IS hard. You're gonna die a LOT. But the game isn't impossible, and each boss gets easier and easier as you play them. You go into a new boss and see a seemingly impossible-to-dodge attack. After a few tries, however, it's like childplay to move out of the way of those projectiles! Each boss has unique attacks, so you'll never feel like you're doing the same thing twice.
The soundtrack is pretty good, but nothing that would make you go "Hey this game's got a brilliant soundtrack" (Undertale, for example, had extremely memorable music for each boss). However, a few bosses would have quite action-packed and fast-paced themes that would really get your blood pumping. For other bosses, it's easier to play while having your own jams on in the background (I reccomend You Say Run extended because WOW, that's good).
The game isn't without any glitches, and some of them do prevent you from partaking in some of the experience of the game. The game can also feel like the controls are janky or uncomftortable, especially on keyboard. For this reason, I would really reccomend you play with a controller. It's much more natural and smooth. It'll feel a lot harder when you play with a keyboard, trust me.
All in all, this game is brilliant, with its art style, gameplay and (sometimes) its soundtrack. I would really reccomend this to any person that enjoys a real challenge (or maybe you just want to get with the trend, who knows?).

This game is one of the best First Person medieval combat games that I have ever played. The graphics are slightly old and not the best, but graphics don't make games bad. If you are new to this game, I recommend talking to people in help chat a lot. You may need to look up a few things to understand it. But there are some story lines and "quests" you can do. But the "quests" are just jobs you can do for money unlimited times. This game is made for gaming PCs. Not your school or work laptop. I don't recommend playing on those because you'll only get 10-20 FPS on lowest graphics and it's pretty much not playable then. Overall this game is entertaining, and you will love it, if you care to spend time with it. The reason it has so many bad reviews is because most of the players don't leave the first town; Tindrem. Criminals and Murderers sometimes go in there for fun. It is extremely annoying to everyone there. So I recommend new players going on MortalOnlineMap.info and using the map to go to Fabernum. It is less populated and has an easier way to get money. It also has the better side of Mortal Online's graphics. It's way smaller and not horrible. Tindrem is full of trolls, thieves, and murderers. So far, I am very much enjoying Fritz Chess 14. While I'd like to consider myself a decent Chess player, I admit I still have much to learn of the game, such as end game calculations, mass attack and defense strategies, and how to not accidentally spill coffee on my chessboard while I play.
Although I haven't found any tools or tips for coffee related checkmates, (Coffee Temperature Gauge, Player Motor Skills vs. Reaction Timing Graph, Coffee Cup Center of Gravity Chart, Coffee Stain Probability Meter, Estimated Remaining Time of Cleanup, etc.) I believe this program is a substantial learning and teaching tool.
In essence, this software is great for improving your game and playing techniques, or even teaching them if you enjoy being a Chess tutor. While you can indeed play a simple game of Chess with Fritz 14, it offers a great deal more than that, from multimedia files that explain the rules of the game as well as rated and timed matches, to differing analysis tools that suggest blunders, better moves and checkmate threats, to even more tools including subtle hints and showing every single possible move and the advantages and disadvantages of each.
I would like to warn potential buyers of Fritz 14, it can be very complex and intimidating to learn all of the programs offerings. I'm not questioning intelligence here but rather pointing out that Fritz 14 truly does go the distance in terms of analysis tools and options, and the time it may take to learn them can frustrate and be off-putting. However, in my opinion, once you learn how it all functions and how you can best use or customize the tools to your liking, it is that much more at your disposal. So, while figuring it all out can be an arduous task to master, I personally think it pays off in the long run, especially for anyone whom is seriously trying to learn and best the challenges that make Chess what it is.
The core game offers several types of 2D and 3D boards, not a considerable amount, but a few. A player can customize the pieces of the set, the board color and style, as well as the background table the board is set on. This is also the first Chess program I've played that offers 3D opponents that can move the pieces with their hands. While I prefer a simpler 2D Chessboard myself, I find the 3D opponents to be an interesting concept, and I certainly appreciate creativity.
From what I understand, the game also comes with a six month subscription to the
website, which offers news, training, a dedicated server for online matches, and likely a good deal more, all revolving around, of course, Chess. I must admit I tend to be a very esoteric individual (I have Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder) and I have not played online. I would have to imagine the community at
is a positive, intelligent and friendly one, however, this is purely my own speculation. All I can honestly say is "Multiplayer" is not really my scene, so by all means, click the web link and check it out if you are interested.
To conclude my review, I would personally recommend it happily to any player looking to go from being a good Chess player to a great one, from a hobby player to a pro player, or even an inexperienced player to a rather competent player. With patience and a bit of mindful dedication, this program offers a considerable deal of training content and much more. However, if you would rather simply enjoy a Chess game or two, there are much less complex, not to mention cheaper, alternatives to Fritz Chess 14.
And I personally recommend caution with certain...malicious...cups of coffee.
Good luck and happy gaming!

Updating from Fritz 8 is perhaps unnecessary: the older version by and large does the same thing.  That said, I have not regretted purchasing Fritz 14 as I will try to establish below.
The newer Chessbase-themed GUI is very nice, but the chief benefit is that it is easier to manoeuvre the database.   That in essence is the purpose of the Fritz chess suite: chess-playing software is ubiquitous and cheaper (and can play a stronger game: see the open-source multi-core Stockfish) but offering native Chessbase Reader (free) support along with plain-English analysis is of greater value for the serious chess student.
In limited games, I've found the Fritz 14 engine to be stronger than the Fritz 8 engine (processing power held constant) but that wouldn't be important really unless I was GM-standard.
Overall the cleaner interface wins the day.  Dispensing the CD-media to enable the Steam experience is also very convenient, and I look forward to taking my Fritz experience anywhere my light laptop can go.

Fritz 14 is an excellent, if confusing, piece of chess software.  The mileage you get out of Fritz equals the amount of work you put into learning how to utilize its interface.  If you want a simple chess program that is both aestheticly pleasing and fun to play against there are better options than Fritz.  However, if you are looking for a robust program to analyze your chess games in minute detail, Fritz is perfect.
The built in chess engines are moderately powerful and sufficient for most players.  Deep Fritz 14 is available as DLC if you want an engine that can fully utilize more powerful hardware.  There are also more powerful (and free) engines readily available online that plug into the Fritz GUI with little trouble.  I have personally been using Stockfish 5 and it has been working perfectly.
If you want to improve your chess game there are few tools I have encountered more valuable than Fritz.

Something you need to know about Fritz is that it hardly belongs in the games category. Think of it less as a fancy chess game and more of an analysis tool for chess enthusiasts.
Every single bad review you'll see for this program is due, not to some defect or bug, but because this is a bloody complex application and it's rather hard to intuit what it is you want to do. Reading through the manual, especially if something doesn't seem to make sense, is highly, *highly* recommended.  If you just want to play chess, and nothing else, you'd be better served by the pack-in games that come with your operating system. The Fritz engine that comes with this software has a low end rating in the 1400s and is absolutely /not/ for beginners!
So what can you use this for? The killer feature for me is the ability to load up PGN-formatted games (I usually annotate them on my phone) and have the engine go through your game and note where and how you messed up. What you could have done better, and so on, using plain english.
This is starting to sound like a sales pitch, but in short, I recommend this whole-heartedly if you have more than a passing interest in chess.

Pros: Strong engine. Awesome online community. Can watch grandmasters games and all tournaments. 6 month playchess/chessbase subscription. Easy chess engine import and implementation. No brainer for anyone who loves to play chess.

Not really for beginners who wish to learn without playing online (but then again, the best way to learn how to play chess is to . . . play chess, not read books or tutorials).
Overall, the cons are minimal and can be ignored. If someone wants to learn how to play chess, YouTube has a TON of free content. Fritz allows for amazing analysis of games, very large chess database (which is easily expandable via numerous file type support) and online kibbitzing with some of the best players on the planet.
I highly recommend this for anyone who is serious about chess.

Tried it when it was on beta and didn't like it. The game had issues and it wasn't the day one DLC.
Tried it when it turned free... nothing has changed.
Some of the issues found:
- No real tutorials : there's little to no explanation on roles of the hunters or skills of the monsters ingame making it easy to be completely lost and overwhelmed thus never knowing how or what to do anything.  Yes yes there are plenty of videos tutorials online but if a new player need to research on how to play a game outside of the game then this demonstrates the flaw ingame.
- Pick up groups are a mixed bag : because of the previous point, the only play mode is joining a PuG thus there's no way to know the skill level of the players you will find. Nothing to ajust or balance teams or to ensure same leveled players can play together.
- Unlocks :  Since it's now F2P, everything is behind an unlock system. Not an apparent flaw mind you but still the longer one plays, the more unlocks one has. Add the 2 previous points and now it's a big flaw. (new players vs veterans)
- Paid players got shafted : this isn't a flaw in the game but more of a black mark on the individuals that made the decision. Since the game got F2P, the players that bought the game previously got a meager amount of "silver keys" (in game currency) for their trouble.
- Big game of hide and seek : the whole concept of the game is just a game of hide and seek : monster runs away and eats whenever it can. Hunters track him. Monster eats more until it evolves. Hunters try to trap it to kill him. Monster evolves another time then tries to kill the hunters / some generator. Timer expires. Rince and repeat. Forget having a story or a campaign or single player missions. This is just hide and seek.
Because of that, I've seen matches devolve into two ways : quick death of a monster or a long stretched out game where the monster evolves fast and makes mincemeat of the hunters. Not very fun either side.
I'm sure there are plenty of fun to be had with groups of friends but this can be said about any games. Since this game is dependant on others to play it, it can turn either a mess of a game (most of the time) or a fun and exciting match (rare occasions).
Lots of content have been removed during the transition to F2P and that is a shame. Heard the campaign was one of the more fun  games and it explained more of the backstory.
In conclusion: stick to other F2P. This game should be left to die peacefully. It failed when it was released and won't revive in F2P. Yes there will be an influx of new gamers to it but after a few painful matches, uninstalls will follow.
F2P now? I want my $60 back.

I really don't care for the changes that were made to this game. I was going to post my thoughts on some of them on the discussions page, but the developer has made posting unavailable on there. So, I'll do it here.
First of all, I think it's BS that you cannot play stealth runs as the monster anymore. Every 20 or 30 seconds they get a "Planet Scanner" that points everyone toward your exact location. Meaning the closest thing to a stealth run is running to one side of the map, eating as much as you can before they catch up to you/scan you, then running back to the other side of the map, and repeating. It's pretty stupid. The random birds worked quite well before for revealing your location; if you were a skilled player, you could get to stage 3 without being seen. If not, tough luck. As it should be.
Also, the one time I managed to avoid the hunters long enough to get to stage 3 (I usually end up just fighting them to the death at stage 1 or 2, and I usually still win at stage 1, which is stupid), then time ran out and I lost a minute or so later? I don't know what that's about. If matches would go long enough to get to stage 3 more than one time, maybe I'd be able to figure it out. I guess you have to make a beeline straight for the objective the second you get stage 3, and you aren't allowed to go around eating to get your armor up before the final fight?
Now, they also removed a lot of the class diversity. All of the hunters get the dome now... which centers on the monster, Meaning you can't just barely get out of the edge of it. And I'm not sure why you have a Trapper class if anyone can trap the monster now... Also, everyone got health regeneration, but it seems like the medic class was massively nerfed in response to it.
Oh, and the little mini-campaign thing is gone. Matches no longer really matter, because there aren't persistent effects between matches based on your previous ones. It's all just single instanced matches. I personally liked the final match of the previous versions, as well as the diversity of objectives and bonuses from the regular ones, in addition to the fact that when you're playing several matches in a row against the same people, you can try to adapt your strategies to take advantage of how they play.
TL;DR: This game has apparently gone down the path of quick, non-tactical run-n-gun, more in the style of a 1v4 CoD than a tactical, team-based game, like it used to be. Honesly, the game would be a hell of a lot better if they had just kept the majority of it exactly how it was, and made it free-to-play. They could still have put in their perks system and skins to get their micro-transaction money. The game is mindless garbage now, imo. I'm hoping they revert a lot of these issues, and I'll enjoy playing this again.

One of those games with a truly unique atmosphere. Dark, brooding, but with some sparkles of hope and belief in higher purpose. Certainly not a horror.
It gives you a lot of freedom: regarding both mechanics (skills, weapons) and story. You can explore many areas in a non-linear way and even skip some bosses, but then you won't get all the achievements of course. Which is not a big issue, because the game is good enough to do another playthrough.
There's a good amount of lore in item descriptions and dialogues. Combined with a huge, labyrinthine world containing many secrets, it's a boon for explorers. The secrets can be easily found without looking at a wiki, though. The game requires some backtracking if you want to explore everything, but backtracking in this game isn't tedious at all.
The combat system is very good compared to other platformers. Requires some getting used to, but you'll be executing combos with ease after a few minutes.
However, you may find Salt & Sanctuary quite imbalanced. Some weapons and spells are far superior than others. Not a big issue as there's no PvP, but depending on which skills you choose you may find boss fights either frustrating or boringly easy. Finding these OP combinations may be considered part of the game, though, as long as you don't use a wiki.
Speaking of wikis, there are many things which aren't explained in-game, like encumbrance system (apparently you get slower after reaching 25/50/75% encumbrance) or damage scaling on weapons. Some items have hidden properties. However, you don't need to know everything to beat the game and you can easily say if an item is better than your current one by seeing if the stats are green or red. One thing worth knowing is that you can invest more than 1 point in most skills (but you probably won't need this on your first playthrough anyway) and that you can reclaim skill points using grey pearls. Also, it makes a huge difference whether you're holding a weapon as one-handed or two-handed.
Personally, I find the lack of in-game explanations interesting, a bit like in most roguelikes. I have checked a few minor things on a wiki or asked a friend, but it turned out it was completetly unnecessary as it made the game too easy. Once you get to know the areas and enemies it should be relatively quick and easy to start a new character and make the same progress, if you're really unhappy with your choices.
One final tip: DON'T PLAY AS A MAGE. It's OP as ****. I defeated almost every boss in just a few seconds using spells. I guess the developers will fix the balance a bit in the future, but right now choose mage only if you don't mind making the game too easy. On the other hand, it required some training to use the spells effectively, but it was rather disappointing to not even see what most bosses' attacks are.
Also, try using a gamepad instead of a keyboard. Some things are easier on a keyboard, but you may find a controller more natural for this kind of game, like in most platformers.
If you're stuck or want to make sure that you're progressing through the game in the correct order, there's an excellent "Spoiler-Free Where Do I Go/What Do I Do Next" guide on reddit.

I'm really bad at reviewing games from this genre because they're so complex and explaining why they're good is very difficult. Some people find Soulsborne/Soulslike games to be absolutely dreadful, some people think they're the best games ever made, but very rarely does anyone think that they're "Just okay."
General information about gaming and both the Souls and Metroidvania genres are required to understand some of these points.
+ It's a 2D Demake of Dark Souls, in the best possible way.
+ Boss designs are far, FAR better than in Dark Souls 2. (Honestly i might even go as far as to say that it rivals Dark Souls 1 sometimes.)
+ It's longer than Demon's Souls, took me exactly 20 hours on my first playthough. Good length for a 20 buck game.
+ Metroidvania elements are handled nicely, you get upgrades that are required to progress the game world akin to Symphony of the Night and Super Metroid.
+ You can wavedash. (Kinda.)
+ Combat is a ton of fun.
+ There's a metric ton of gear and different types of weapons.
+ Bonfire system is better than in Dark Souls.
+ There's a passive skill tree system similar to Path of Exile, it's interesting and fits the game well imo.
+ Multiple endings.
+ Support for local co-op...
- ..But not for online co-op. :c
- Some of the bosses are quite cheap.
- There is no map, why? 2D Navigation doesn't work the same way that it does in Dark Souls.
- While there is definitely a good replay value here, the lack of online features waters it down a bit.
- Artstyle that ranges from ugly to downright beautiful, contrasts the world a bit weirdly sometimes.
- Too many enemies with grapple strikes.
- Lackluster soundtrack.
- Cthulhu mimics tbh fml smh.
In the end, i will say that this is without a doubt one of the top 3 indie games i've ever played. You should definitely check it out if you can. When this game shines, it shines bright.

I've played this game for awhile, since Early Access. If you're a fan of games like Contra and Metal Slug, this is the game for you. The 2D run 'n' gun gameplay brings back that old retro feel for gamers such as myself.
The game itself is pretty solid with a decent bit of content. The game brings together two of my favourite games and meshes them together surprisingly well. The gameplay of Metal Slug with a gun crafting system that evokes the feeling of Monster Hunter. You even go on missions in a Monster Hunter-ish format. For those who aren't familiar with one or either of the aforementioned games, Mercenary Kings is a 2D side scrolling run 'n' gun adventure where you take on the role of "King" or "Empress", one of two members of the titular Mercenary Kings, a group of heroic mercs out to stop the dangerous organization CLAW.
The graphics, sounds, and gameplay all give that retro feel but retain mechanics not often found in older games. One such system being the crafting system where you can make an almost infinite combination of guns. Want to make a gatling gun that has the range (and possibly accuracy) of a sniper rifle that shoots acidic bullets? You can do just that. The mission difficulty curves rather well and, with over 100 different missions, this is rather impressive.
The missions themselves all follow rather basic procedures. Enter the map and fulfill objectives. These range from "neutralize" (destroying or capturing a boss target), "eliminate threat" (destroy all enemies within a certain area), "gathering" (find the specified quantity of a specified item), and more. While the objectives are more or less the same, the game manages to throw a few curve balls with special variants, such as bosses guarding target areas or different permutation of enemies in a given area.
While this game is a great play by yourself, it's even more fun if you can play with friends. You and up to three friends can take on the evil CLAW! With this, even more possibilities open up. Do you and your friends split up and take on several objectives at once or do you stick together and back each other up? Will you all bring in LMGs and Shotguns in preparation for a lot of close quarters combat or will one of you pack a sniper and pick things off from a distance?
But not all is great for this game. While it's an amazing game either solo or with friends, playing solo does feel a little punishing. When solo, you may have to do some runs almost perfectly and that requires repeating a single mission several times (which can get dull). But with friends, it won't nearly be as bad, Missions like this, however, are few, and a little practice is always good, no?
It's definitely worth a look. This game may not be for everyone, but if you like arcade-y games like Metal Slug or Contra, this game is for you.

Mercenary Kings is one of the few games that depicts how only a few mechanics can throw a monkey wrench into what could have been a great game. From the start you are given a game that is a mix of Monster Hunter,Metal Slug, and a dash of Gears of War. In theory this sounds quite awesome! In practice it shows how each one of these mechanics can work against each other.
Starting with the Monster Hunter mechanic of finding loot to craft new guns, this forces the player to grind in a side scrolling shooter. At first it dose not seem to be an issue up until you face the 2nd boss in which kill you. Or in most cases, will time you out. Causes you to replay stages for better weapons because bosses in the game can run away from you if you don't kill them fast enough. Next is the two other mechanics described in which can work against each other.
Due the reload mechanic you will be taking shots and you have no way to defend yourself. This could have been fixed with an instant reload rather than the timed reload. Adding another layer of frusteration. I tried going in wanting to love it. Even through the time on greenlight I tried holding hope. Sadly I can't say it is fun sadly. I give Mercenary Kings a 6.5/10.

While not a strong player, (I not played chess in years) my main experience of chess programs have been chessmaster and some free programs. While Frtiz 14 program on steam has had its fair share of issues, they seem to be mostly fixed now, so what do you get with the steam version of fritz 14?
You get Fritz 14 GUI
Fritz 14 (single core engine)
fritz 11 SE (also single core)
crafty 23.05 (multi core engine)
Video beginner courses
Fritz 14 opening book (weighing in at 449 mb (not sure how many openings)
2013 database weighing in at 809mb and has nearly 3 million games
lets check database (subscription based)
and 6 months access to Premium membership to
,
So for those wondering the difference between this version on steam and deep fritz, well the engine on the steam version is single core only, (apart from crafty) hence the lower price, otherwise I think there is no difference.
One thing I should point out is, while I do recommend the software, I don't recommend it for those new to chess, learning the basics, there are better ways to learn chess, Fritz is aimed at those that already have skill with the game, and want to go farther. So if you are a rank beginner and hope that Fritz will teach you the basics,, basic tactics and want good tutorials, I would look else where.
While Fritz does have training modes like Friends mode (which auto adept to your strength and play style), Handicap and fun, some opening and end game tutorials (as well as a few others) sparring mode that you can set the level 1400 up to 2480 and handicap position (removes pieces from the board) there are a few other modes too.
there are a few visual help options like spy, opening hints and so on.
Then we have a very powerful features of Frtiz, Full analysis mode and blunder check, (also have a infinity analysis mode too)
Two feature I just noticed, Fritz can also play chess 960 (where the chess pieces are randomly placed and with some extra rules) and givaway chess, (you are forced to capture any attacked pieces) these modes can be fun and access by the little down arrow on new game in the home tab)
You have a lot of options, so describing them all would take a lot of work. I'm only really covering the main features.
One thing I must mention is the extremely poor help file, it's just plain horrible, and doesn't really explain all the features of Fritz that well, even the PDF file seems to be more cut and paste from help file or vice versa, so some features (or many) might leave you head scratching on their purpose. So when you do start using the program, I highly suggest you check out videos done by Steve Lopez, as his videos have allowed me to understand a lot of features which would otherwise be unexplained or never used.
another aspect I will mention, Fritz does support UCI (Universal Chess Interface) engines, (free and commercial) so you can easy add more engines of your choice, (stockfish for example (which is free)
I think I will wrap it up by saying, I think the program deserves an 8 /10, but you should only get it if you know chess pretty well, but you also should only get this version if you not got a recent version of Fritz, as you may not see that many differences, (feedback from other players who have owned Fritz 13)
so after that, I don't think I have much else to add.

For context, Fritz Chess 14 is my first foray into a chess application with such a rich feature set.
Fritz Chess is a tremendously deep chess program capable of world class play whose creation dates back to the early 1990's and whose lineage includes computer chess wins over IBM's Deep Blue prototype.  The engine itself is separated from the interface which allows for custom engines including
(accessible from within the program).  The included engines are Fritz 11 SE and Fritz 14 (default).  The programs capabilities are wide ranging and far too numerous to completely enumerate here and depending on your expertise you may not exercise many of the features accessible through the interface which brings us to the question, is Fritz Chess worth the price tag?
The Steam version of Fritz Chess, "Fritz 14", is a single core application as opposed to "Deep Fritz 14" which is multi-core and more expensive.  Therefore, for the price Fritz Chess 14 provides a welcome nominal discount as most non-advanced users will not require nor miss the multi-core support.  The Steam version has single core support but leverages 64 bit Windows natively and thereby provides an optimal experience.
Opening Fritz Chess for the first time, especially if you have not been exposed to such a chess program before and no Chessmaster does not count, can be overwhelming.  As soon as the interface is displayed the player can instantly derive that Fritz Chess is a feature rich, high value chess application.  I'll enumerate the features available just on the "Home" tab.  The other tabs being File, Insert, Board, Training, Analysis, Engine , View and of course everyone's favourite; "Help", which you'll be in dire need of if you ratchet the difficulty too high.
"Home" consists of: Paste Game, Paste Position, Copy Game, Copy Position, New Game, Cancel Move, Replay Move, Move Now, Resign, Offer Draw, Stop Clocks, Infinite Analysis, Blitz Game, Long Game, Levels, Hint, Suggestion, Threat, Coach is Watching, Database, Edit Game Data, Load Next Game, Load Previous Game.  The feature set can be overwhelming to new users though a help file is just a click away, however there is no manual available via the Steam download nor on the store page.  An oversight which should be fast tracked and corrected.
Casual players are in for a real treat as Fritz Chess will no doubt help you improve your game.  Under the Training tab there are a wealth of training options such as but not limited to Opening and Endgame Training though I would like to elaborate on two additional modes.  The first, Handicap and Fun which is essentially as the name implies, a handicap mode.  This mode consists of many sliders such as Playing Strength but more importantly Fritz Chess comes equipped with a multitude of pre-sets ranging from Careless and Moron to the upper tier opponent skills known in the program as Steam Roller and Assassin (misspelled in the program's interface as Assasin).  These pre-sets can be individually fine tuned allowing the player enormous flexibility.
The second option, Friend Mode is more of an adaptive artificial intelligence that consistently always plays just somewhat better than the player.  Combine these modes (or just plain old New Game) with the ability to turn on the program's help system allowing for the display of recommended moves (and moves not to make) plus a comprehensive database of more than 1.5 million games and you have an extraordinary learning tool.
To answer my opening question, yes, Fritz Chess is a good value and Fritz Chess is not only a tool that you can learn from but given it's engine customization features it is a tool that will grow with you as well.
Edit: Sept 22, 2014 - The multiprocessor engine is now available as dlc.

This is likely the best MMORPG that exists at the moment. It stays true to the RPG component of the genre - unlike certain titles that produce highly streamlined, monotonous, instant-gratification gameplay which seem to hand out gear and don't rely on a community aspect at all. All things in the game are player created and player run - the gear, the politics, many of the buildings (castles, towers, etc) throughout the world, even. I must say, if you're a very casual player you may not see the point in putting time into this game. If you are easily frustrated by being attacked by another player, this is not the game for you. If you are interested in a very challenging world where you must learn to defend yourself and your party from any possible lingering threat, where nothing comes easy, and where a battle could break out anytime, you've found what you're looking for.
I would liken Mortal Online to Ultima Online in many ways. The game has a complex skills system which allows you to build a character the way you would like it built, and leveling is much like it is in Skyrim where by performing actions, you gain the levels. The world is a largely open-ended sandbox, allowing players to do whatever it is they desire, assuming they have the necessary ability, and guilds and solo-players alike wage war and create conflict anywhere in the world they see fit. Crafting has so many different levels to it, and you will find that it is best to rely on other characters to fill in some of the gaps that you are missing when it comes to combining components of each individual crafting system (from people who took different skill line paths than you) to produce something greater. Collaboration is very much key in many components of this game, which I think is vital to an MMO's success.
Some things unique to Mortal Online that may entice you:
-Mounted Archery (Mounted combat in general)
-Taming of beasts/mounts and breeding of those beasts to produce better creatures
-Dark open world dungeon delves (that anyone might join on or interfere with)
-Graded hitboxes (where you hit your target and what they are wearing there is taken into account instead of damage being weighed against all armor worn)
-Fully lootable player corpses (with the exception of their banks)
-Pickpocketing other players (pay to play only feature, but makes sense)
-Many secrets hidden around the world that can teach your character strange and powerful forms of magic.
Understand that while the game is free to play, and while free to play characters are capable of achieving plenty, free to play characters are limited to 60% of the maximum efficacy that skills can provide (60/100 effective points in skills is your maximum). I would strongly suggest giving the game a try, since it is free to play, and if you're interested in seeing the heights you can achieve with maximum results enabled, subscribe and join a guild to play with.

Overall a well put together casual solitaire based card game with an engaging theme, and plenty of levels to work through (presumably 50 states x 10 levels each).
As you work through levels you earn money by stringing together long sequences or matching suits, which allows you to buy extra bonuses such as being able to see some of the face down cards so you can plan ahead, wild cards which you can use to either extend a streak or save to ensure you can get that last card for the perfect clearance, all of which give you more strategic options and reduce the feeling of just relying on luck to win or lose, which can be the downside of solitaire games.
There are a couple of mini games that also pop up randomly (making burgers, fixing leaky pipes, match 3 desserts), they don't really add much but I guess they break things up a bit and they don't take long to clear.
If compared to Legends of Solitaire (similar game from the same developer) it is probably even more casual (you can't fail a state as a whole, only individual levels if you don't collect certain highlighted cards), and much more polished.

Not too short and not too simple, but very enjoyable and very addictive work...
Probably this game is the best solitaire on Steam.

I acquired RAGE on a sale, and for the price I paid, I'd recommend the experience.  The world is gorgeous, in a post-apocalyptic, Fallout-like style, with some obvious Fallout-like ripoffs.  Still, it's worth it just to experience some of the really immersive visuals.  The characters and people are reasonably good, beautifully crafted, fully voiced with a variety of personalities (even if some of the acting is forced).  Also, the first "Dead City" experience was really memorable.
The game is largely good, but suffers from a lack of direction and from trying to do & to be too much.  The crafting system is interesting and provides some value, but largely unnecessary to complete the game.  The various minigames, too, are value-added, but in the same way that finding spare change in your pocket is value-added.  The vehicles actually drive very nicely and are enjoyable, and the vehicular combat isn't bad, but the entire racing circuit side-game is virtually mandatory and--as such--is a detriment.
The game is arguably broken up into three sections, by "hub".  The first and third sections are really short, while the second is probably over-long.  The first section, being short, makes sense.  Its an intro to the game; the starting quest hub.  The brevity of the third hub, however, and the entire third section of the storyline--including the anticlimactic end stage and ending--feels shockingly unfinished, especially compared with some real gems in the section section (Wellspring), most notably the first visit to the Dead City.
Ultimately, I'd recommend the game, if only to experience the first half to two-thirds of it.

Combat is whack-a-mole with the humans, and fast-zombie with mutants. Speaking of the enemies, half of them dont drop any items and those that do only carry $2 and 3 bullets on their person- bosses don't drop anything. Almost all locations are recycled twice in an effort to pad-out the game. Speaking of content, the DLC is just content that was cut for the game to be resold, and gives you the privilege of playing past the campaign end.
Some closing thoughts: the game has abysmal texture pop-in, is capped at 60fps, and has multiplayer achievements that are now basically unobtainable. Oh, and there's no map. You're expected to know where everything is by heart. The Wasteland Legends copypasted the same locations a THIRD TIME!

Quick summary for this game is unless you want to waste some time and shoot things, I dont really recommend this game.
Now for the detailed explanation:
Quests work like this: you must get item, bring it back, do it again. Storywise this game is lackluster at best. The setup is OK; you wake up from cryostasis and find out that your in a post-apocalyptic future. After that the story never really picks up and by the 3rd act it drops dramatically. The ending is also very anticlimactic; you turn on a machine, short cutscene is shown, and credits roll (not even a final boss) not even telling you what happens afterward. Half of the gameplay is FPS which is fine but no real variety of enemies. There are three real types of enemies you face: ones that are fast and melee you, ones that are generic grunts with guns, and ones with a lot of armor and heavy weaponry. While the enemies get tougher, your weapons do not. you can find yourself wasting a whole rifle clip to kill one enemy, and the  only way to bypass this is to buy stronger ammo making all normal ammo obselete. The other half of the gameplay is driving. Controls are a bit iffy, but overall its fine. You can do races to upgrade your vehicles, but I found myself ignoring these as you can get where you want rather quickly and suffer little damage. Most sub weapons you use only once or twice except maybe for grenades and wingsticks which are usually one hit kills. The game as a whole is very average, the graphics are fine, controls are good, and it for what it does, it does it fine. Would I recommend this game? No. Really if your just looking for a game to kill some time, this game will do it but not much else.

Directions can get sketchy sometimes if you're easily disoriented or checking out a new area for the first time without realizing that it borders another previously explored area. Still, the map is pretty well laid out, and even without using fast transport, walking from anywhere to anywhere else isn't too punishing.
I wish there was a respec option. Even with a penalty, being able to try new builds without starting a wholly different character would be very much appreciated. Still, the flexibility of the tree is nice - reminiscent of FFX's sphere grid. The little bits of lore on each node are nice too, for those who enjoy that kind of thing.
A word of caution: some NPCs give quests that cannot be continued if the NPC isn't found and chat options exhausted before fighting the area boss. This can also happen in some rare cases where bosses may be fought out of "order." Just check the wiki perhaps, if completion in this manner is important. Winning the game and building properly are not dependent upon it though, so it's more a matter of collecting all the acheivements, lore, and crafting mats.

Alright, let's talk Salt & Sanctuary.
Welcome to the two dimensional version of Dark Souls that will have you writhing, groaning and begging for more.  Taking a page from the generic "masochistic" platformer and implementing the theming and basic game mechanics from everyone's favorite challenging medieval "kill things until you get killed, repeat until satisfied".  Salt & Sanctuary is an excellent source of enjoyment for anyone who lives in either of those metaphorical apartment complexes.  The intriguing blend of scarce plot and heavy gameplay that forces the casual player to rethink his life choices and gives the keyboard warrior a chance to dance in revelry.   All styles of player will find an enticing challenge as they march through the choatic wasteland of the mysterious island that tells a better story in twenty odd hours than a certain tv drama can do in six seasons.  Not to say that you NEED to remember the story to enjoy it or whatever you bought this for.  Maybe there's a girl on its production team you want to impress so you bought it and left it running on your laptop to log  "play hours" overnight so she'll think you are a fan.  Hey, i'm not judging.  I've done a lot more for a lot less.  Anyways, if you are considering jumping into the pit of gleeful frustration, think no further.  You won't regret buying this game.
