How to play the goliath in beta: don't.
If you play as the goliath (or any of the monsters for that matter), you cannot win no matter how hard you try; as long as hunters stick together, which they always do, you have no chance of winning. I literally have a better win loss ratio on Pacman than when I'm playing the monster.
Hunters have around 1600 health (which is more than you think, more on that later). You want to target the medic first, because they heal other hunters so fast that it is literally impossible to kill other hunters. Do not let the medic be revived, because reviving restores way too much health (80%, then 60% max health). Then you want to kill the support, because they give other hunters armor, which basically, also, makes it impossible to kill other hunters. Then you can choose to kill either the trapper or the assault. The assault is meant for dealing the most damage to the monster, nothing else; the trapper is meant for, well, trapping the monster. Their harpoons are probably the most annoying thing to deal with (next to Abe's statis grenades which stick to surfaces and have a large radius and long lifetime); if you do not break them, you cannot move, let alone escape.
That is if you can get past stage 1 to begin with. If you are caught in a dome at stage 1, forget it. Spread your monster buttcheeks and take it, because that is what Turtle Rock wants for some dumb reason. If hunters have 1600 health, which is unrealistically high, why do monsters have to eat so much in order to regenerate armor (not health), let alone be able to evolve? You would think the monster does more damage to compensate for their high health- nope! Quick attacks only do 90 damage, heavy attacks do 250, and moves do anywhere from 50 to 500, which is a joke.
One thing about trappers is that they also have another role: recon. The trapper can tell all players which direction the monster is with a push of a button (probably the 4 key), which makes hiding to feed to regenerate armor and eventually evolve practically impossible. I like the idea of following footprints in order to find the monster, but I guess camping was so much of a problem in alpha they had to introduce spammable tracking. It is such a cheap but unfortunately the only way of playing the trapper, it ruins the monster experience and the game in general. Your victories as a hunter will feel so empty after winning 10 times in a row, which is extremely easy to do.
Back in alpha, only the trapper can put up a dome, only the medic can revive others, and hunters in general were not overpowered. Did I mention there were, gasp, NIGHT MAPS? Well, not anymore; all of that changed in the beta (aka Evolve Stage 2). They wanted to make the monster not a braindead character to use, but what ended up happening is the hunters became braindead characters instead. It takes literally no skill to play hunters, but it is almost impossible to play the monster and actually win.
Turtle Rock, fix your game. This is why you have mixed reviews on your unbalanced and unfair game.
By the way, if you're good at playing monster, good for you. I'm not you, however, and this is my experience with the game so far. I want to love the game, but I felt the need to complain in hopes of convincing the developers to rebalance the game. Some of us get monster despite setting it to the lowest priority, I on the other hand main the goliath in hopes of improving my monster skills to circumvent the unfairness of the game.
Also, I would prefer the silver coins to be more accessible, be it via micro transactions or a larger payout postgame.
Don't get butthurt because I don't recommend the game just because I "suck." There is clearly a balancing issue and I'm not the only one who thinks that, hence the mixed ratings.

Evolve. I loved Evolve. Let me tell you a story my father told me. When he was young he got a pinball machine for his birthday. He loved that thing, not only was it cool but it made him cool (what with it being the equivalent to a VR headset today). But like all things, it got a little stale. So he took a break from playing with it for a while. After three days of not touching it he came home and noticed it was gone. He asked his father what happened to it and he told him that he gave it to a neighbor kid because he thought he didn't want it anymore. Today, I know his pain. I haven't played evolve in a while, sure, but I still loved that game. I made so much progress: unlocking almost all the achievements, getting all but one of my medics to legendary, and not to mention the fact I bought all the monsters and characters. But today, none of that matters. Evolve has basically become one of those Iphone games that you see commercials for on T.V. but you think to yourself that they have no business on T.V. Today, all progress has been erased, Achievements, levels, character skills, stats; all of it gone. Hunt and arena are  the only game modes now and all the skills are based on spending fake Iphone money. You can earn Iphone money by playing matches or completing daily "quest" complete enough quest daily and you get more money and unlock special prizes. You use that money to buy skins and characters and level up your skills. (you should begin to see the comparison). Overall, this system could have been great for just the skins alone, but the skills did not need this. I know making this a whole new game on steam would have been a little weird, but they forced us into this new version and took everything away without our word. This game is dead to me now, perhaps I shall come back to it, But I'm not ready to just rebuild what I had spent so long to create.

Overall I like this game. It teaches you the basics of surviving. Staying hydrated, having food, and keeping warm are all very important things to learn. That being said, the hunger dynamic needs adjustment. Humans can go 3 weeks without eating, yet the character will constantly get hungry and need to eat at least 5 times a day. I think the game should focus on rationing your food more. It seems that my main concern is eating all the time. It breaks immersion for me. Also some levels have unclear pathways and/or boundaries making it confusing where to go. Having a compass would help greatly. Wolves are another issue which can be tiresome. They are constantly coming after you. You eventually have a gun but ammo is extremely rare and needed for hunting eventually, which is why being hungry all the time is such a problem. Therefore the only way avoid wolves is to, as the games says, "give them a wide berth". However, this does not always work. I had a wolf chase me from behind and all I could do was fight it off, taking damage. How many times can a person get attacked by a wolf and live to tell about it? In my experience, about 3 times before I died. So the main challenges in this game are eating, avoiding wolves, and staying warm. All in all not a horrible game but I feel certain dynamic elements should be addressed and improved. Finally, the storage capacity for your backpack is extremely low. Yet a myriad of tools are offered to the player which weigh a lot. The game is all about exploring and these tools help the player do that. I feel the weight capacity of your bag should be increased by another 10 kilograms. Then the player can explore more thoroughly and not have to backtrack to the same place which can be come redundant.

I know it says I played for 1.2 hours, and frankly I'm shocked it kept my attention for that long.  I've long known the Unreal Engine was trash, almost akin to the horrid Arma engine the bug-infested, clunky tragedy known as DayZ is built upon.  I thought, "Well these people have made a game that some speak highly of, it seems to be riddled with awesome features and I love the freedom described.  Maybe they actually made something good out of UE!"
...  Nope.  At first it wasn't bad... although running felt like walking, and sprinting felt like... walking.  According to the built-in "GPS" arrow navigation... "thing", I calculated my full-on sprint speed at about 1.3m/s.  Iunno about you guys, but my 5 year old can sprint faster than that.
But I got over the twelve minutes to get to the first "quest" giver and was finally able to draw my sword and try my hand at the combat.  Wasn't bad, I gotta say.  Killed a few piggies.  Actually put a little faith back in me... so I did another 12 minute "sprint" to the town gates and was given a bow for returning captain whats-his-name's dagger. (Actually wanted the dagger, damnit...).
I equipped the bow and 25 nub arrows, thought to myself "Awhhhhh this is gonna be sweet!", took aim at a tree about 25 meters in front of me for a nice practice shot, and as I held the LMB to draw the bow, my characters arm did some wierd bending backwards thing like he was trying to grab his elbow.  Just looked downright goofy.  I thought, "Oh god, really?"...  I released the LMB to fire my arrow at full draw...  It went about 10 meteres and hit the dirt at a 90 degree angle..  That's right...  Either gravity is excessive in this midieval world, or the bow and arrow I was given as my starting weapon is basically a twig with a rubber band drawstring.
Not to mention the noob help chat (Nifty feature btw) was literally OVERRUN with people complaining about the high level, veteran players slaughtering them everywhere.  Between the horrid graphics, absolute lack of detail in the character animations, overcomplicated interface and what I feel is simply a lack of effort on the part of the developers making this game, I honestly don't understand how they can sell subscriptions for $14 a month with a straight face, nor can I understand why anyone actually buys it.
To each is own...  If ya like it, ya like it... but if you're thinking about trying it, just know this is basically a shining example of how bad Unreal Engine really is.

Alright, I previously had a bad review on this game.
What can I say? The first impressions were less than great, especially when I couldn't log in the game for any apparent reason for months.
Oddly enough, the next day after posting that review, suddenly I'm able to log on. Coincidence?
So, after actually getting to play and experience the game, here's what I have to say:
First, I'm sincerely glad I gave it another try. The experience of this game is like none other, that's the truth.
The world of Nave is a bittersweet landscape, a twist of beauty and terror. You can explore EVERYTHING, you can FIGHT everything. However, EVERYTHING is DANGEROUS.
Swimming is dangerous, pvp is hell, standing in a desert or blizzard is deadly, your friends are deadly, the city guards are out to get you if you aren't careful.      This game should be titled:  50000 ways to die in an MMO.
The enivronment is gorgeous.  The land is huge, the water is breath-taking (literally), the sky is awespiring, the cities are quite regal (Though I wish we could enter more buildings than a bank.) The Music is very attractive and helps you connect to the game.
The combat system is an amazement. Some people say it's basic and boring,  I say it's quite tactical.  In WoW you can macro everything you want to do to a single key-press and spam it.   In Mortal Online, you have to AIM for weak spots with your weapon.   The combat of this game is more engaging than ANY I have encountered, even in console single-player games.
The major downside of this game is that the community is very, very toxic. I recommend finding a guild as soon as possible to help remedy this. (Shout out to my HERO friends!) After joining the HERO guild, they immediately took me under-wing, taught me more about the game and have been very patient with me.
There are some limitations to the game for free to play players.  However with enough skill, know-how, and knowledge of the game itself and what gear it has to offer, a F2p can go toe-to-toe with a P2p any day. It's all about reaction time and accuracy.
Soon I will begin toying around with construction, we'll see how that goes.
Apologies to the developers for my harsh words on my first review of this game, (frankly it was deserved with 2 months of unavailable play.)  But it's okay. The game speaks for itself, and I'm glad I get to be a part of it.
Keep doing what you do, StarVault.

As a fan of the Trine series, the hype train surrounding Trine 3 made me nervous. Zoya is less fun! The game is short! The depth (literal 3d depth!) is awkwardly excecuted! Said everyone.
Zoya does play a little differently. Amadeus has much more potential than he used to. Pontious feels at home. My wife and I frequently switched characters while solving puzzles, and I feel that's a testament to them being a little better balanced.
The Chapter selection has a wonderful ambiance, which helps the story unfold quite nicely. The level design feels fantastic - except for when it doesn't. The levels are cohesive and immersive. You really musn't be afraid to walk toward the screen, or all the way in the back just to look around, or you might get hung up or lost in a silly spot.
The end of the game did feel abrupt. It's less of a cliffhanger, and more of a sentence that got cut off, as if expectations and development time took very different turns than originally planned.
All that said, My wife and I had a lot of fun over a few nights. Though the game felt short, we really enjoyed ourselves. If playing single player only, or paying full price, I wouldn't recommend this. If on sale or planning to play with someone else, I would definitely recommend picking up this title.

Let me start off by saying how much under rated this gem is....
Rage is a very unique first person shooter set in the post apocalyptic Earth, after a massive asteroid has hit the planet. Due to the toxicity released upon impact, some humans have turned into 'mutants' where as the remaining lot has hidden underground or in some sort of shelter. With time, cities have been build from scrap left around where as most of old buildings were abandoned. You emerge into this vast wasteland to discover humanity working to rebuild itself against such forces as bandit gangs, mutants, and the Authority – an oppressive government regime that has a special interest in your character in particular.
This game can be compared to the Metro series, although having played both, i must say the combat in Rage is a lot more satisfying. The abbility to craft, sell and buy items is really cool. Just like in Metro, you have to buy your own ammunition which adds realism. You can customise weapons, improving accuracy, damage etc. You get to participate in car races, upgrade your car, add weapons to it, carry out quests like in a standard rpg. The world is not huge, but large enough, missions are difficult and very interesting. There is also a lot of gore.....u can actually blow other peoples heads with a sniper rifle :D
Overall I highly recommend this game to any fps fan who also is in to the post apocalyptic atmosphere, likes to explore, gather resources and enjoys a bit of melee/gun combat brutality. It really needs more positive reviews, because it deserves it 100%. I r8 8/8 xD

The Long Dark is an extremely detailed game about winter survival. Your winter gear has stats including temperature buffs and windchill reduction, you take injuries in specific forms like broken ribs or strianed ankles (injuries all require different remedies), you attact more wolves by carrying raw meat or when bleeding... just when you think you found flaw with the game mechanics, you realize that its already been accounted for and it goes into more depth than expected. For example, you are not only slowed by being overencumbered, but are more likely to strain an ankle, fatigue faster, and burn more calories!
Wintermute (story mode) episodes 1 and 2 took me greater than >30 hours and was very engaging. At first it serves to teach you how to survive, but later takes on a bit more interesting plot. The survival and challenge modes are grueling and excellent are providing a different kind of challenge than the story does.

Hello everyone, this is my review for "The Long Dark". Ill tell you what you need to know, after playing the Storymode for a while (it's a sturdy 19-20 hours) I have seemed to fall in love with the game. Right off the bat you're met with BEATIFUL scenery, some will say that the quality of graphics are terrible, but they are truley stunning, and very unique. Just like all of the other reviews, the game is TAXING when it comes to your survival skills, you must amount to crazy odds and be very persistent. There are no bases for you to build, just random homes and a town or two that you will find, during the Storymode you will be greeted by two individuals, whom you must help and in favor will help you, but they set up lot's of TEDIOUS quests for you. The game focuses on hunting, and quick choice making and "The Long Dark" makes you think, it makes you learn from your mistakes, it can be an unforgiving environment. Their are three difficulties, a Storymode and a Survival mode, and currently nine regions, all accessible by going through tunnels, all explorable without making a new game save. "The Long Dark" is beautiful, it has it's scary moments, and the game will suprise you, when you are not paying attention, ask the pros . . . it doesn't matter how skilled you are, you will always be taken down, after a sum of time. I bought the game when it was $15.00, it's base price when not on sale is $35.00, I would currently say, GO FOR IT! The Hinterland team is going to add more to the Storymode, we just have to give them time. Not many bugs, or any I have found, nothing wrong the music, it's beatiful, although I do wish their was more to the Survival aspect, like being able to BUILD YOUR OWN SHELTER, or to HOLD OUT AN AXE, or MORE WEAPONS. But as the game is now, I think it is worth it, completely.
Thank you for reading - Carson

As good as (or better than) many other SHMUPs avaialble on Steam. You have a dodge/teleport button, a super button, etc. The direction of your attacks is automatic (straight ahead) so aside from orienting your ship in the right spot to take out the waves of enemies and be aware of your own hitbox to evade their many attacks there's not much to the gameplay. The level design can be a little bit bland, consisting of little more than a solid color and some grid lines or lasers to dodge. Although the levels progress in a "constantly viewing the horizon approaching" vertical shooter kind of way seen in other games of the genre, the game often has a cool effect of exaggerating how much this is "rolling" toward you, and often tilts the horizon to make for an interesting effect while progressing.
The game provides various enemies with different attack patterns to mix up the gameplay often enough, and you are able to select to swap your weapon or keep the one you have at level's end after defeating the big bosses of each stage. The soundtrack inparticular is good, and the announcer adds to the game's overall well-done arcade-y effect.
I do wish you could upgrade your weapons or super by collecting pickups during the levels, but I have liked most all of the weapons you can opt to pickup at the end of the level. The dialog's humor while funny at times (seeing a boss simply titled "Mother♥♥♥♥ing Spider") begins to become one-note (titling the boss right after that "A Tiny ♥♥♥♥ing Planet") The standouts of the game for me are the boss fights and the soundtrack, as the soundtrack thumps along and you dodge the bosses' screen-filling attacks. I'm a fan of the new retro wave esque soundtrack so that probably adds immensely to how much I enjoy the game, but if you're a fan of the retro SHMUP genre I think you will probably enjoy this game.

Warning: Possible spoilers. For 20 bucks? Hahaha. No. Lets start with the singleplayer. Let me just start by saying this game is no where near "story driven". The story is generic mess, with unbelievable hard to remember characters. The game really fails to draw you into the enviornment and really does a poor job of character development. If there is any. Most of the in game dialogue is just "good shot partner" and "nice kill". The rest of it is just you being scolded by your commander. The animations are incredibly janky and so is the voice acting..oh god the voice acting. Player models are compressed messes as well, and every enemy pretty much looks exactly the same. There is no more than two different player models for each type of enemy you face. The game also tries to dish (And I am assuming) heart wrenching drama by showing you the acts of genocide comitted in the Balkans in the 90s. To be honest, it was so generic it was very hard to take it seriously. The main villian is dull, and quiet weird. (Not in the good way) I saw myself constantly skipping the cutscenes, and just trying to get the missions over with. The "bossfight" is just some dude with aimbot. The game really is not challenging, and the detection system can be quite laggy at some points. You could be crawling on your belly in the bushes and be detected or crouching in the middle of a road and pretty much be a ninja. Overall I would give the story a 5/10. At some points it can be quite fun, but most of the time it is just dull, and feels more like a mini game or challenge instead of an actual story mission.
The multiplayer is a bit of a different story, that is if you can find a server. I found that getting kills was quite satisfying, but lag and poor hit detection seemed to ruin it alot. Customization is probably the most disappointing thing about the MP. All you can do is choose a gun out of like 5-7 max, and a random player model from the story. I've been with the series (and Paradox games) since a long time and I'm glad this one turned out to be great. Currently it's 3 months after launch and this game runs better, faster and more stable (I had not a single crash) than it's predecessor runs now. In my opinion, this is the best HOI.
People complain that it's too mainstreamed and easy, but I don't think so. The game is still very complex, but at times easier to use. Automated army management can be turned off, but is useful at times. As Italy, I put a general on auto, gave him targets in Africa, dumped some crap units on him and let him conquer bum♥♥♥♥-Africa while I micromanaged the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of my offensive against the Soviets.
The new factory system (IC is gone) is much more believable. Your man don't change but their equipment does as your technology improves. It's more realistic and palpable to see your men putting down their Great War Rifles and pick up some machine pistols. You are in a constant struggle to supply your front lines with up to snuff stuff, which really gives you a feeling of fighting the ressource war, which WW2 actually was.
Yes, there are downsides. The AI is sometimes crazy stupid, but it will most likely be improved over time as they did with the former HOI's. I also can see what people don't like about the new air combat, but it's fine for me.
This is a great game which will entertain me for a long time. I can't wait for improvements and DLC's. Paradox did a great job on this one. Definetly Recommended.

Really really good game, it explodes to the max the artstyle from Trine franchise. Yes is not anymore a side scrolling 2.5D platforming video game. But its fun and well made. Some times the camera is a bit crap,,, but the game play is fantastic.

In short, if you love Trine 1 & 2, you'll probably like Trine 3 as well. It's beautifully made, but the gameplay will leave you wanting. Get it in a bundle sale, since the 5 hours of gameplay are not worth the full $20.
Compared to the first two games, this is a tough change for me. Since there is no leveling and no skills to unlock AT ALL, Trine 3 misses that spark to solve puzzles creatively. No more anti-gravity fields, magnets or surfing planks to get that experience orb up high. I get that the 3D engine makes all those skills hard to manage, but this effectively makes most puzzles feel the same.
It's not all bad though. The music is good and the levels are gorgeous, especially the 'drawn art' levels. The fact that it's in 3D also makes combat a lot more interesting. The story is alright, even though the ending clearly had one or several expansions in mind.
Overall, I think most people will enjoy this game. If there's a bundle sale, get all three parts. You'll love Trine 2, and will enjoy the other two.

This game deserves a lot more heat than it got.
I loved Fallout 3/New Vegas; and this game is very similar to that but with vehicles.  Looks just as gorgeous if not more so in a different way.

Ask yourself the following questions:
If you answered at least one of those with "yes", then RAGE is for you. It's not as complicated as Fallout in terms of role playing elements, exploration, but the atmosphere is very close (why wouldn't it, be, it's Bethesda's work). It's not as stylized and as fas paced as Borderlands, and you don't get quite that amount of different weapons, power ups and items.
What you do get are beautiful graphics, a very well designed, post-apocalyptic envrionment, a larger, customizable number of behicles you can drive around in, and shoot at your enemies with, but also race other drivers with to gain perks, new equipment etc.
The jobs you can do (or quests) are fairly varied so far, and although in-game money isn't thrown at your in abundance, you usually earn enough to afford necessary upgrades and ammo to keep going. Driving requires a little practice, and the camera can be a little bit of a pain when driving, but overall, the experience is great; especially the feeling of speed.
One of the best aspects of this game are the cool weapons. The changing of ammo types which requires your protagonist to modify the weapons in real time by slotting/fitting different modules to a base gun is just awesome. The railgun you get is also hands down the best version of that type of gun since Quake II. However strange that may sound, but rail-snipering someone from a distance is a strangely satisfying experience.
Technically the system requirements are correct. Any quad core with a fairly recent GPU can handle this game at HD without performance problems. The game's not installed on an SSD, so that's why, but it's barely noticeable.

Sanctum is a hybrid FPS tower defence game. Build and upgrade your towers between waves, and then assist your towers with killing the invaders before they destroy your base power core. The combat feels like a fast paced old school FPS. The two elements fit together nicely, for example some enemies take reduced damage from  towers until the player shoots their weak spot. And of course each different tower is better suited to killing different types of enemies. The environment can be a hazard to the player - fall off a ledge and enemies will push forward until you recover. This all allows for some varied and deep tactics. The number of maps, difficulty levels and achievements provides for many hours of replayability. The graphics and sound quality is good for an indie release, and the game is also very stable and bug free. The only major flaw is the lack of any kind of story to tie the levels together. But Sanctum is still great value for money, even at full price.
It’s simple to learn, hard to master, and impossible to put down.

Lovely Planet, despite looking like a nice, child friendly game, is hellishly difficult. It takes pro Counter-Strike players, swallows them whole, and ♥♥♥♥♥ them out as a shell of their former self. Casuals should just leave now, go find something else to play, there's nothing for you here.
Lovely Planet has a great, soothing, fun soundtrack; this was a nice design choice to help prevent players from raging, because you will die, a lot. Tight controls, mixed with lightning fast gameplay make for a high skill ceiling, and you'll nearly need to reach that ceiling just to 100% the game, let alone COMPETE on the leaderboards.
There are 100 levels, each one containing 3 obtainable stars:
-1 star is given for completing the level, usually pretty easy, but sometimes can still be painful.
-1 star is given for beating the par time on a level, in the earlier levels you could be a complete numbskull and still get par time, but on some of the later levels you will need nearly frame-perfect play.
-1 star is awarded for having 100% accuracy, if you've got an itchy trigger finger just forget it, you won't get this star. You'll need to snipe falling targets from hundreds of feet away while flying through the air yourself, and remember, miss even one bullet and you won't get the star.
Easily the Dark Souls of FPS games, and in my opinion, Lovely Planet is the Dark Souls 3 that we all wanted but FromSoft didn't deliver.

It's a rather controversial game. In my opinion, it's far better, than its only rival, the SniperElite v2, but it doesn't make it good. The graphics are okay, the story is ridiculously simple (and bad), but the athmosphere of the game is more or less good.
The creators learned from their earlier mistakes. Not learned enough, but learned. The game finally more good than bad, and I find this improvement promising. Finally enemies can't see you from 200 meters while you crawl under a bush, and most of the times they act like a human being... No, that was a little strong word for it, so let's just say they smarter than the CoD enemies.
And why it isn't an especially good game? First of all, sometimes it's anoying as hell. There are many times, where the save point is before some unskippable scripted event, and we have to watch it over and over again if we couldn't be succeded at the first time. And there are situations where we have to try a section for a several times, because it's literally almost impossible to find who do we need to shot. The levels are bigger, than they were in the first game, yet they still too linear, and too much part of the game we have to follow our spotter, who (by the way) doesn't worth anything when it comes to fight. If there are two enemies, he helps us to kill one of them, but other than that, he almost never shoot, and doesn't even cover our back. Luckily the enemies see that he's such a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, so they don't shoot at him, even if he runs past them. And the last problem is that the game is rather frustrating sometimes. The best example for it is the final "bossfight" if we can call that this way. We have to fight with our nemesis, a traitor, an other US sniper, which is literally means the following: we are proning at a lookout, and searching the area to find him. That's all. Sometimes he shoots at us, so we have about 30-45 seconds to find him, before we die. The tricky part is, the area is FRAKIN' huge (imagine an area which is about 250-270 degrees wide, and there are buildings between 300 to 1100 meters), and the boss shows himself only when he shoots. Of course we can't move to an other spot where he don't know exactly where we are. The game doesn't even let us to let go the riffle and take a look without the scope to see the glimpse of sunlight of the enemy's scope. So the final bossfight is only about luck. If you don't watch exactly the same spot, exactly the same time when the boss shoots at you, you won't find him. If you are lucky, you find him at the first occasion, if you are not, you'll try a hundred times, and you still won't see him.
They put multiplayer in the game, because nowdays even a frakin' SIMulator of a CITY can't live without multiplayer, so how an FPS could be? It was just a waste of the precious worktime, because doesn't worth a damn. Snipers against snipers, so it's boring-boring-boring. A co-operative multiplayer might work, but the competitive one isn't a good choice for this game. You literally watch the area, looking for enemy snipers, and you are happy when... no, not when you kill someone, you are happy even when you finally see a player from the enemy team.
Since there aren't many competitors for SGW2, I recommend it but not for everybody. If you are a usual FPS player, then you won't like it. It's for sniper fanatics only, and even they won't be satisfied with it, but as I said: there aren't many games with this theme :/

Graphics - I have an old laptop, so unfortunately I have to dumb down the graphics a bit on games like these. Even still, it was very good at dragging you into the environment. I am looking forward to the day when I buy my new computer and I can play this game again with the graphics on high. :)
Enjoyment - 5/5 I have over 250 hours in this game, some of that is achievement grabbing but most of it is playing through the main story and the DLC. It was great, and I am looking forward to Dishonored 2.
All in all, it is highly recommended.

I really wanted to like AC2. Having heard great things about the series, I chose this as my starting point and was a bit disappointed.
There are so many poor development choices here, and I'm really hoping they're addressed in other AC games because I'd like to try at least one more out. But here are my criticisms:
1) The game uses Uplay, which sorta sucks. I thankfully haven't had a lot of the issues some of the other reviews here have had with it, but I did run into issues on initial startup (some Uplay files deleted themselves and I needed to reinstall it, for example)
2) Freerunning..while it's pretty awesome and can be at times fantastic, there have been a lot of situations where Ezio just did the stupidest♥♥♥♥♥♥and really frustated me. Trying to jump off a roof towards a hay stack and for some reason jumping two feet out onto the cold hard floor and dying. Trying to drop two feet onto a balcony to get a treasure chest and INSTEAD jumping 30 feet down into a haystack. Trying to catch someone on a rooftop and jumping slightly too far off to a side instead of onto a little foothop. You get the drift. In a game where you need to be swift and precise the precision just doesn't feel there quite a bit of the time...Not that often, but often enough that it gets frustrating. Along with that, the puzzles aren't even really puzzles, but more of a "can you look around and then hold the freerunning button in the correct direction".
3) Combat is atrocious. Foes are constantly blocking and sometimes counter you (which doesn't hurt you much, so there isn't really any reprecussion) so you have to whittle down their health tediously or just sit around waiting for them to attack so you can counter, which sometimes barely hurts them. Allies hit each other (had a quest character hurt another one 3/4 of her health). Stealth killing sometimes launches you off roofs when you just wanted to look cool..Also random posts get in the way when you drop in for stealth kills. Why wouldn't it just make me jump differently so the stealth kill worked? Who knows.
4) You can't switch weapons or armor without going back to your main villa. This is stupid as hell. If I buy a weapon that is worse than my old one just so I have everything bought why do I automatically equip it and why do I have to go all the way to a transport station so I can get back to the main villa, go to the equipment room, and reequip my better weapon/armor? So stupid.
Some of the dialogue is just laughable (you need outlets Ezio 'I have outlets' OTHER THAN ♥♥♥♥♥♥S haha lol) and the plot is a little contrived. I'd much rather just have the plot center around Ezio and not have the simulation aspects (also the decoded video segments are ridiculous looking and stupid in my opinion). Following people around for missions is boring. Money comes way too easy and you'll have more than you ever need after you start upgrading the villa. There's no sense of tension since you can heal yourself at any time.
The game isn't all bad of course. There's still some fun to be had and there's plenty to do and collect. It just seems really pointless at times...there's enough playtime here that you'll 'probably' get your money's worth, there's just plenty of better things you could be doing or playing.

THIS GAME IS NOT FOR EVERYONE!!!
Reading the reviews people have put on here I agree with some but most of them are the persons fault. Yes the game pretty much made a 2d Dark Souls but it's still good.
-Controls-
Yes this games controls are odd and the timing is not perfect. There is a slight delay in jumping which will cause troubles when it comes to platforming (which causes a lot of early game deaths) but it's something you will adjust to without realizing it.
-Bosses and Enemies-
Most of the bosses have♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥me off but they are still fair you just need to learn the moves. Unlike Dark Souls where you have a whole 360 degrees  to dodge around the bosses the 2d makes it a lot harder to dodge but they balance it out by giving you a faster dodge. The normal enemies can be a pain most of the time but just like bosses after you learn there moves they are easy.(Besides those unicorn ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s, I hate them with a passion.)
-Getting lost-
The one I have seen people complained the most about besides controls is getting lost and backtracking. This is a metroidvania game, you are ment to get lost and backtrack. This game will not hold your hand when you need to figure out where to go and will not tell you when to backtrack but it will drop small hints here and there.
-Game Mechanics-
The game pretty much tells you what you need to know but just like Dark Souls there are hidden game mechanics that they won't tell you about and neither will I.
If you can get past odd controls, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bosses and enemies, getting lost , backtracking, and hidden mechanics then you will like this game.

The long dark is an realistic apocalyptic survival game where you could chose to do story mode or try to survive on different difficulties and maps as long as you can. Would rate a 10 out of 10, but only if you have time on your hands to progress further in the game.
If this game was cute girl I'd really try to avoid hitting her really hard.. cause its pretty and stuff..

In short, the game is very buggy and its very easy to get a bad save or be stuck in your game.  Animal AI is kinda bad and the UI is a bit janky.  Also the game fails to simulate one of the most critical elements of any survival scenario: multi-tasking.  That means in this game that you can only do one thing at a time such as boil water, repair clothes, sharpen knife etc.  Other survival games seem to model this correctly, not sure what this game's problem is.
I quit at a point in the story when you have to fight a bear, but you can't be smart about it, the game forces you to face it multiple times regardless of how much you prepare, or how good a shot you are, by making the bear effectively invicible.  Also in my game the bear spawned right outside the cabin that I got the quest from and I got mauled before I could react.  Very buggy, leaving a poor impression.
Also if you play the story mode be prepared to lose a lot of hard earned loot as you can't go back to certain areas, or containers will become basically inaccessible.  Resource management is already a pain, its a shame to lose 20kg of meat and the ammo you used to get it.
Overall I was having fun until I saw the wizard behind the curtain, so to speak, so I thought I'd spare you.  Maybe get it on sale or wait until they fix the problems.

Much like the previous games, Trine 3 is a physics based platformer which looks great and has bags of character. The big difference between this and it's predecessors is 3D movement which (suprisingly!) works quite well for the most part. You will have the odd death due to the extra dimension and exploration can sometimes lead you out of bounds, but the game is forgiving with its checkpoints and it's unlikely you'll have to play whole sections again due to this.
It is not a particularly hard game - getting all the achievements is ridiculously easy - but the journey is enjoyable and is sprinkled with some clever ideas and puzzles.
On balance I recommend Trine 3 because what's there is fun, just be prepared to be left wanting more because in reality this is only 1/3 of what the game should have been. Probably best to get it when it's on sale.

I admit, I am no fan of puzzle games. I got this in a bundle and it has cards so I gave it a try while the cards dropped and I was pleasantly surprised.
The story, although borrowing from a lot from popular movies, is quite original and also engaging. You play the female protagonist, the partner of a private detective in the 1950ies, investigating in a remote and kind of rundown asylum with a troubled past.
The characters you encounter are well written and come alive quickly, even though most converstations are short (which I appreciate). The interaction with the NPCs and your partner is pleasantly natural and logical and mostly well voice acted. The cutscenes are animated well and the pace is fast enough to keep you from skipping through them.
Also many of the puzzles don't seem out of place (as they often do in these games), you have to do a lot of repairs, piece things together and often come up with creative solutions to overcome obstacles. Even on casual (which I played) the help is not too obvious although you can completely skip larger puzzles. The option to play mahjong instead of clicking all the items in the collection puzzles is also a nice touch (there are even special achievements for the mahjong games). The "what happened here" puzzles are also adding to the variety although personally I felt them quite boring.
The only major criticism I have is the price: 8 $ for a game that is finished in 2-3 hours is just to much. But if you spot it in a bundle, you can count it as one of the games making the whole bundle worth buying.

Wow, I was plesently surprised by this game. Overall, if you like point and click or hidden object games and want a game the fuses them together awesomely, this is the game for you.

Lovely Planet is a first person shooter. Only much more than a first person shooter.
In this game, you run and gun your way through a simplistic, abstract, and cute world, clearing stages of baddies as you dash for the goal. It doesn't sound like much, but there's a lot more to it than just running and gunning: You have platforming to do, gimmicks to use/overcome, baddies waiting around corners and behind walls ready to shoot you, and one challenging road ahead of you.
And this game is indeed challenging. While, like most games, this game starts out pretty easy, you'll eventually be jumping from platform to platform while shooting down baddies at the same time. Some levels may take you many tries, but I found it impossible to get mad at a game like this with super tight controls for a 3D platformer, a responsive, "fires as fast as you can pull the trigger" semi-automatic... gun... thing... simplistic but nice looking levels, and fast-paced action, all with a super upbeat and energizing soundtrack as the cherry on top.
Even if it's just 5 worlds, it's a blast to playthrough, and it's even more fun going back to levels you've completed to beat your previous times and find secrets. Not to mention after you learn the levels you'll eventually master them and become a gun-slinging speed demon. It's worth the $6, and can be a good time killer, or just something to do if you don't have any other AAA games to be getting to.

I played this game on the Xbox 360 when it originally released but never finished it for some reason. Today I finished it for the first time and HOLY CRAP! I love this game!
The missions are structured very well and give you many options to complete your objectives. The gameplay is very fun and, just like the rest of the game, gives you a lot of options to develop your character. Want to be a silent ninja who is never seen, heard, and non-lethally takes down his enemies? You can do that. Want to be a bloodthirsty assassin that murders everyone in sight no questions asked? You can do that too.
The story is a typical revenge story, but it is told really well and does have some surprises. The game also has three different endings depending on your actions throughout the game. I got the good ending while trying to kill as few people as possible, but I can't wait to start a new game and go on a murderous rampage to see how that ending plays out!
This game does not punish you for how you play and instead actually encourages you to play the way you choose. This was a breath of fresh air when the game released back in 2012, and it is still a breath of fresh air today in 2016.
If you like first person action games, stealth games, or games with non-linear gameplay, buy this game. You will not be disappointed.

Let's start this off by saying that I am a sucker for tower defense games. You could give me any TD and I could play it for hours. With that said, this tower defense game throws in some new ideas along the classic TD playstyle. The first thing any player will notice is that there is an AI partner with you throughout the campaign. He has a great voice, has emotions, and has a sense of humor. I felt for his past loss and wanted to help this guy out. The main campaign takes about 8 hours to beat and I believe there are around 15-20 maps. Each map has multiple accessory challenges that add an enormous amount of replayability. This TD can also be quite challenging and is one of the harder TD's I have ever played.
----
As with most Tower Defense games, some towers are clearly more stronger than others while some towers are completely unnecessary. Defense Grid does make an effort to try and fix that but it didn't completely work. Don't get me wrong, I still used every tower in every map but I think that just added more difficulty to an already challenging game.
----
This is one of the better tower defense games out there and it even has a storyline that the player will actually care about. If you enjoy tower defense games, definitely pick this up.

In what felt like the longest 6 hours of my life, I've experienced a whole new genre of gameplay, which was smooth, fun and honestly quite refreshing in today's gaming market. When I first loaded up Cuphead, I immediately was struck with nistalgia from the "Looney Tunes" and "Walt Disney's Fantasia" days. The art is very consistent and has a very familiar feeling, looking very much like the old cartoons I grew up with, yet having it's own fresh, smooth and bouncy style to it.
Getting into the gameplay, right off the bat I got a nice mix of, what to me seemed like, Mario, Metroid, and Metal Slug. If you've played any or all of those, then you get the idea of how this game plays. You side-scroll through each level with 3 lives (at start) defeating or avoiding multitudes of varying and challenging foes. The trick is, though, that these foes will mostly, if not always, have a movement pattern to them. What this means is you have multiple play styles available to you. You have the option to blast your way through with your 2 primary attacks and your Super attack, which are changeable and can be purchased from shops between levels. (This option is of course much more risky, but does not require precise movement and memory to clear the stage.) Your second option is to learn the patterns of the enemies movements and attacks, and dodge them accordingly, which will save your hearts for the end of the stage, where you'll need them. Now if you're wondering, "Why will I need my hearts for the end?" the answer is simple and it is also one of the main selling points of this game. Similar to Metroid or Metal Slug, once you clear past all the normal, yet challanging enemies in the stage, you will be put up against a Boss. Each Boss is unique and is themed according to the stage scenery and layout just as the normal enemies are. (Ex: Garden stage= Bug and plant enemies and Boss.) These boss fights aren't your average "Drain their health" boss fights, though. In these boss fights, the boss will have a few different stages of varying attacks that you must dodge AS or BEFORE you attack them (depening on the boss, some you can attack while dodging, others you cannot). When it comes to attacking, your damage and accuracy don't deal damage neccessarily, but they actually determine how long each stage of the boss fight lasts for. It's more about progress than damage, so staying alive is most important.
This game, aswell as having amazing gameplay and stunning graphics, tells a short simple story of two brothers with a gambling problem who are out to reclaim their souls from the Devil, yet does it elegantly and almost effortlessly as you have fun blasting your way through big bosses. The story isn't shoved in your face, rather slipped in-between stages, and really makes the game flow beautifully while not sacraficing any story details or taking you out of your immersion in the Cuphead world.
Long review short, this is a must-have, one of a kind game that really brings back childhood memories of cartoons, while also creating some awesome new ones. This is a long needed refresher and I'm ecstatic to see an old genre reborn in the new age and done so flawlessly, mixing the old cherishable aspects of the original side-scrollers with some new age flavor and color to it. If you're considering this game, consider no longer, it will be worth your every penny (this game is worth more than $20 to me, honestly).
And remember people, Don't Deal With The Devil ;) ~(Except in this case)~

I didn't even realise this and bought it thinking it looked epic btw.
Basically what you have in this game is only 2 modes. You have a story mode called 'winter minute', which is a bit of a mad name to give it rather than calling it story mode? So anyway, you start the game, and it's a plane crash in Canada in the winter. Now you survive. That is basically the story mode. It gives you purpose (somewhat) and very indepth guidence, softly teaching you about the different elements of survival which are actually, very interesting.
For example, one of the most basic things in the game is to make a fire. You can use a bit of newspaper to make some kindling to catch a flame from a match, then put that in a pile of twigs = fire. You can then add bigger bits of wood for the fire to burn longer & hotter, which subsequently wamrs you up quicker or dries wet clothes quicker. Every time you do this though - it takes time in the game (sped up for you as the player). You can start a fire quicker by using lighter fluid with the rest of these ingredients. This kind of thing imo is really interesting as a fresh concept for gaming! There are a lot of other things you either craft or make use of, all along the same lines as making a fire.
Once you've mastered the basics & from the get go, you feel as though every deicison you make is on the borderline of life & death...and it's a great survival game without the typical zombies. Instead, you're battling against hunger, thirst, tiredness & some wild animals...
But shortly into the story you then begin to have basically enough of everything and surviving isn't a problem, now you're thinking what type of food shall I eat for dinner and what foods should I just stash in X location. It's like fallout or skyrim where you stash everything that you don't even need because you MIGHT need it at some point...even though you wont lolol
So after you have more than enough stuff, the story turns into stupid bizzare missions. When realistically you would backhand someone in that situation and say WTF mate why would I do this pointless thing for you when I need to do something more important. Doing pointless missions and removing the element of survival really takes away from those first 5 hours or so of the story where you genuninely feel like you're struggling.
As well as doing pointless missions, when you are told these missions half of it is in cut scenes and half of it is text you press A to go to the next block of text (if using xbox pad - which does work fine with this game btw). Obviously the logical reason would be that they then added extra dialog into these scenes...which if it wasn't finished why get it voice acted and move beyond just text? Doing pointless missions to force you to go from point A to point B, then back to point A...for no real reason and a lack of connection to the story just seems like a half hearted way to put a story together really. And the story mode isn't even finished. They have I believe now 3 episodes out of 5 released for this.
For me personally, I'm upto a point now in the story where I am basically set for life to just live where I am. Doing more pointless missions just seems pointless. Cons:

The second part of the 9 Clues Series, “The Ward”, takes place at a psychiatric hospital. You and your partner, both detectives, get a call from a doctor there and arrive to find the caller has died under mysterious circumstances. You must now solve the murder, and the secret of Mnemosyne Asylum.
As per usual with Artifex Mundi games, the background art is simply gorgeous and detailed. The character art, when still, is fairly good, however it’s not the best of their games, and the animations are… let’s just say they leave a lot to be desired. It feels a little like they’ve almost gone backwards on this aspect. The music (most times creepy) and sound effects are, as per usual, good; the voice acting is unremarkable, which is good in that it is, at least, not bad.
The story isn’t overly original, pretty typical to most HOG games and to Artifex Mundi in particular.
The particularity of the 9 Clues series -and what sets it a bit apart from other HOGs- is the “Detective Mode”; in it, you are made to find a certain amount of clues in the room, and once you do, you are made to put them in order to recreate the sequence of events that occurred there. It’s an interesting change and nice addition to the typical HOG scene, as you’re not really told what you’re looking for exactly, but if you have common sense, it shouldn’t be difficult anyway.
While this is not too different from other ‘find the sequence’ puzzles, it’s a nice change of pace.
Just like other HOGs from Artifex Mundi, however, it continues to have the same downsides. For instance, you’ll need to find 3 items, but you can’t put one into the puzzle already because you don’t have the other two. Or things are in slightly ridiculous places or require to do slightly ridiculous things when any sane person would’ve just used something else that was handy. You can’t really escape those issues in HOGs, for the most.
There was also a very lol-worthy part on the game where you literally find a to-do list on placing a bomb and making it go off. Erm. Seriously?
Something I did really enjoy though was that this one had less backtracking to be done. Most the items you needed for any given section were within one or two rooms from where you were, sometimes even in the same one. Still, with Artifex Mundi backtracking hardly makes a difference, as they have fast travel through the map (speaking of which, the map icons aren’t as nice as in their other games, it made me a bit sad).
With The Ward, they’ve gone back into allowing you to replace Hidden Object scenes for a game of (wait for it, I can never spell it) Mah Jong. The rest of the puzzles found throughout are fairly similar to their other games, some a bit more challenging than others.
There are lots of collectables to be found: phantom objects, clue symbols, model fragments… it was nice, but it also started to get a bit annoying to have to be looking out for all of these.
If you’re a fan of HOGs, and a fan of Artifex Mundi, I definitely recommend this one.

Trine 3 is certainly different from other Trine games in the series:
- No leveling up at all
- 3D environments (situational)
While I can see SOME complaints being valid, generally, the game is well done:
Pros:
-3D spaces make for some very different levels
-It's Trine. So if you liked it before, it is more or less the same idea.
-Steam workshop (for levels!)
-Art design - especially the "drawn" levels. Just beautiful.
Cons:
-It is sometimes hard to gague depth when travesing levels, which can result in cheap deaths.
-Some levels *cough the solider's (pontius) survival challenges are WAY harder than the rest of the game.
-It is pretty short.

This is hard.  I mean, I love the other Trine games so much, and this still has mostly the same charming environments, characters, etc.
However, by adding a third dimension to the gameplay, it seems like they ruined the controls, physics, combat, etc.
How about this, for example;  near the end of the game there's a log bridge that is all stored away and presumably you have to use Amadeus to free it.  In the first two games, this would have been a simple task;  magic it out of there.  How it's presumably supposed to work is the same in theory, however, in my game, none of the logs could be moved by magic.  I spent the better part of 5-10 minutes creamming a block in there to try to wiggle the log out.  Even then, that didn't work, but I did have enough of a gap to fit Zoya in between the bridge and the wall.
Countless other issues arise because of the way the controlling of physics-enabled objects works now, and the wonky hot-spot/targeting system for Zoya and Amadeus.  I had boxes go flying off into space, boxes that mysteriously become immobile after touching certain objects, etc, etc.  It was maddening.
The fact that the game just ends roughly halfway through is a giant kick in the balls, and now Frozenbyte says "we're done with Trine now, maybe we'll revisit it down the road".  First they sell this game through Early Access, then they stop halfway through and now they're just bored I guess.
Whatever.  I guess they were super pumped to direct their efforts towards a Thief ripoff and a Magicka ripoff.

Step into a steampunk wasteland where Fallout meets a Mad Max type of world with a great inventory and an even more interesting crafting system! This FPS has some of the best AI that I have ever encountered. Not to difficult to battle against, but not too easy either and for once fairly smart as well as crazy. Id's graphic engine that they used is pretty, traveling the wastes and looking up in the sky is quite a treat. There is a lot to do in the game and neat places to explore through missions. It is somewhat open-world with a more linear style approach to the side quests. Lots of customizing to play style from adding different sets of things to vehicles to make them stronger as you travel and even lots of choices when it comes to weapons. With 4 weapon slots you have the ability to make some choices as to buying/creating different kinds of unique ammo and what weapons you want to carry. You can also build turrets that come in handy and a little spider like robot that follows you around offering some much needed assistance along the way.
Even though this game is a few years old, I recently put some more time into playing it and I am really glad that I did! I used to have a GTX 560ti and the game didn't run that great. I played a little and noticed some settings weren't able to turn up all of the way. Now upgrading a few months ago to a new GTX970 (which I love btw) has shown huge improvments no doubt. Rage does have its flaws like all other games out there, textures close up are a bit messy, for me the sound breaks up when driving in the wasteland and I have stumbled across a few glitches that I just have to reload my game.
Some of the graphic/sound qualites that I have enjoyed are light shafts when walking down narrow areas, the lighting plays off of the walls nicely and adds a great ambiance to the game. The sound inside of places like sewers where you can hear the dripping of water from pipes really draws you in, (I have a pair of 7.1 dolby headphones and they pick it all up!) Another cool thing that I have enjoyed is when you are in a firefight and bullets hit pipes and steam ejects from them. Just another immersive detail that I wanted to point out.
Overall I would buy a sequal to this game in a heartbeat. It was fun, kind of weird/scary at times and lots of steampunk areas to explore. The character design is really AWESOME, huge fan of the art and style of the game. Give it a go and I am sure you will enjoy the story as much as the intense AI that offers up a refreshing challenge!
Word to the wise, load up on ammo when out on quests and make sure your vehicle is ready for action! Just like any FPS title out there ammo is essential. You need it, you want it and if you want to make stuff go boom boom you, gotta have it!
Have fun! Rage is a good time!

There was a time when tower defense games asked you to do one thing – set down defense structures in order to prevent waves of enemy units from destroying your base. All of this was done from a top-down view so that you could see the action without really being in the midst of it all.
While there have been recent attempts to change up the genre, like Defenders of Ardania which allowed players to build their own armies, such games have stuck to the top-down perspective and not changed the formulaic gameplay. Other games like Plants vs Zombies, for example, fully embraced the old mechanics but were very successful because of their presentation. Yet only recently have games such as Dungeon Defenders changed the perspective.
Sanctum offered me a first-person view of the tower defense action becoming the latest game to do so. No longer having to watch helplessly from the sky and pray that my strategically placed towers would fend off the enemy, I found myself able to take part in defending my base right in the thick of things.

In The Long Dark you will get to experience how much of an enemy nature can become when you are suddenly thrown in the middle of nowhere to survive. This game does not hold your hand. There are minimal instructions and hints, the challenge starts right away - the fight for your life. Although the graphics are not realistic, the atmosphere and nature still are. The interesting part about the story is that also that you are in the aftermaths of an apocalypse. A very silent, calm apocalypse, but a deadly one. It is not very apparent at first, mut makes sense later.
This game can't be hurried through, the distances you have to travel are very long, the nights you have to spend tending your fire are very long. If you sprint everywhere you burn more calories and become tired faster. You have to plan out your expeditions. Supply-runs can become tedious with a full backpack and growing exhaustion. A crazy snowstorm might appear out of nowhere. A bear attacks you while you are looking for hidden caches. No weapons? Try to hit a rabbit with a freaking stone for 6 hours, so you don't starve.
The game mechanics work well, even though they take some getting used to. At first it was hard to get started because of the minimal instructions, but it also made it more realistic. A slightly faster walking/crouching speed would really save a little nerve. Then again, being from Finland myself, I can truly say that walking around in snow is not fast business.
Overall, this game is immensely fun and demanding. I have never had a similar experience in a game and I can say I've enjoyed the challenge very much. The storymode is quite interesting as well, there are some mysterious things to explore in the frozen and silent apocalypse wasteland.
I truly recommend this game to anyone! It's very lightweight and has easily 50h+ playing potential.

The Long Dark is a beautiful, expansive survival game that takes place in the brutal winter wilderness of Canada. The sandbox mode is entertaining on its own, with a variety of things to do and places to explore. It was helpful to me especially as I navigated the maps and learned the game mechanics. However, I returned to the game after some time due to the release of the new story mode, which left me curious about the characters' history and the mystery behind the phenomenon that caused their plane to crash at the beginning.
While many survival games have a pattern for success that is easy to determine early on, The Long Dark requires its players to be smart and strategize - one mistake can easily leave you spiralling into starvation or deadly hypothermia. However, this game is full of options and there are so many ways to achieve success. Your survival method and how you approach a problem can be an entirely unique experience from player to player. This is also a game where the environment changes constantly, based on weather patterns and the movement of animals. All of these aspects lead to a more realistic experience overall.
The game stands out from other survival games because of it's art design, atmospere, and lighting effects. Winter is personally one of my favorite seasons, and this game truly brings out the beauty behind the frigid cold.
Without the story mode, I found the gameplay to be very solitary. This can be a pro or a con, depending on the type of player you are. While it increased my sense of immersion and truly highlighted the feeling of what it is to hunt and struggle in the wild, it also made me feel lonely. But, I assume that is the point.
While the survival system is intricate and detailed, some components are forced to unecessarily create difficulty. For example, clothing and equipment degrades very quickly as you use it. The player must consume huge amounts of food and water to sustain themselves from day to day. However, these may be necessary mechanics, or else the game could be too easy. There does seem to be an abundance of resources, so I have to assume this balances everything out. At times, I felt all of the tasks I had to do in order to survive were tedious and without payoff, especially with how much I had to keep feeding my character, but for me the Story Mode provided enough reward.
This game reminds me of an uglier version of Fire Watch. Just buy that game.

Some games cause rash. A rash you can not scratch. And when you don't get more of the scratch to the itch that plagues you, you end up sitting in a dirty street, cooking up a bottle of Jenkem over a burning trash can, injecting it into your worn out cockvein. This is not a review about a game that helps you, but one that only makes you just a little more broken.
Salt and Sanctuary is a strange game. Many people say this is the lovechild of Dark Souls and Castlevania: Symphony of the knight. I beg to differ in this judgement. After playing and completing this game I can say that this felt more to me like a mixture of ghost's n' goblins regarding the visual athmosphere, mixed with a platforming experience close to Ninja Ga(y)iden and a combat system like final fight, all dipped into a semi deep RPG manager with a rather large world you need to explore without any map whatsoever.
Apparently this game was created by a 2 man development team consisting of 2 brothers. That is to say rather impressive. The last game with such a small dev team I played was Dust:Elysian tale. And coincidently it was an Action RPG like this. Seems like those are a go-to place for Indie devs. Not complaining though, at least not about those 2. Well, maybe a little. This game has no story, and what little of rudimentary tropes there are fly directly out of the window the second the game finishes the tutorial sequence with a supposingly impossible boss fight against everybodys favourite tentacle monster, never to be seen ever again.
A thing I have to give Salty Sanctuary is, that it appears to be a highly customizeable game. You can play a caster, a ranger or a knight, even with slight variations inbetween each class competently, resulting in a completely different game experience. That, and limiting yourself even more if you wish to a no-magic mode, nude mode, or even if you so desire (no idea why you wanted to but hey) a permadeath mode.
I played this game like so many other on PC with keyboard and mouse while my character was a medium armored knight with a big weapon. I refused to use magic and was able to conquer the thing without ever using a shield. Not gonna lie here, the first 1 or 2 hours into the game were so bad that i contemplating requesting a refund for this. For some reason the menu management is really bothersome. When i tried to acces different screens or option menues those windows usually closed when i tried to browse them. Almost anytime when i was trying to use the mouse, the game refused to register the clicks or blended the mouse out of the screen, which caused me to end up more then once buying several units of items not in one stroke, but buying them one by one, sometimes several dozens. It sucked. The presence of of monetary currency that is not "Souls" left me dumbfounded, as many of the items you can buy for money stop being useful 2 hours into the game. Next time just say each and everthign for salt.
The combat system is fittingly deep. You can chain weapon combat of smaller arms together and juggle opponenets around while big weapons usually oblitere them in one strike. The combat is meaty, full of blood and explosions. Quite fun. Dishonorable mention: The hitboxes. This game has one of the worst problems with hitboxes I have ever seen in a game. It's even worse than Dark Souls 2. Usually it's enough not to hit the enemy, but the thin air before him. Many enemies have difficulties judging your attack reach as well. This is all topped of with an almost useless dodge roll that has no invincibiliy frames whatsoever. You can still manage to win the game with it only, I am the living proof of that, but its more difficult than it needs to be and the utility is just not present in the same magnitude as you would expect it for a game that is shamelessly dickriding on the success of dark souls. Some of the bossfight were either also flat out boring or ridicously imbalanced (With one or two of them so much dysfunctional that I am willing to give a golden♥♥♥♥♥♥♥award for one of the most broken ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t bossfights in my entire life), but honestly said, the combat with those is rather mixed up most of the time and you can tell that the dev trieds really hard to make the frequent boss battles as interesting as the limitations of a 2D engine would humanly allow. So I am willing to forgive that. With the exceptions of Bosses stealing Souls and not giving it back when you defeat them. That needs to change.
What little music is in the game is pretty nice. It fit's the athmospere of the game and sometimes even gave me flashbacks to ye good old diablo 2, when you listen to guitars being stringend at the sight of some nicely piled up corpse mountains. However, therein lies the problem. There is not enough music. At all. When i finished my first playthrough i felt like i only listened to maybe 6 tracks, excluding a brief and exclusive track for the final level and the unique theme for the final boss. Here's hoping if there will ever be a S&S2, that it has a significant bigger track library. Hopefully even with NPC voiceacting, because that is sadly missing as well.
Overall visual design of S&S deserves praise. It's very good, with a small exceptions. The enemies, bosses, weapons and armor designs are top notch. There's a lot of them and they are all clearly distinguishable from oen another. Given some of them are flat out stolen from other games and rebranded, but they all look nice, faithful to the golden age of videos games in the 16 bit era. The Player characters and friendly NPC's do not get a cut from that cake. They are flat out ugly and look like anorexic deformed aborted cat fetuses, You can customize them but thats like putting a pig dress and painting it with make Up. It remains a pig, no matter how you look at it. This goes as far that some of the characters even get grossly distorted eye disabilities as if there was an invisible carrot floating over their head that genuinely freaked me out the first time I saw them. Luckyly you don't have to endure that for long, once you get a full encased helm to shield your eyes from the butt ugly mug of your toon, so that you have a splendid time exploring the dark and depressing dreadful landscapres to their fullest extend. I would say that the world feels, just like dark souls 2, like an amusement park of atrocities, but the well connected and vastly different from each other levels actually do make sense within the content of the game. No spoilers though.
The game is surprisingly big for it's price. To the point where I wondered how many more hidden corridoors the devs could have put behind gated walls. If you like exploring, you will like this a great deal. Not explicitly the most difficult 2D game I have ever played, as the nature of a grindy action rpg bites itself in the♥♥♥♥♥the more knowlegdeable and skillful you get and your gear advances. But thats what NG+ is for.
If you like a RPG game with considerable jump-run episodes, above averge difficulty with reward-faktor of if you like to insert some nasty burning♥♥♥♥♥♥into your urethra from time to time, you can consider this pleasantly presented brawler with a price tag below 20 Euros as recommended. Remember: Winners don't take drugs. Except Jenkem. That's 100% natural. Good Evening.

Yeah, I like this a lot. For one, Niko is a precious child that I want to protect and the game is able to evoke emotional investment simply out of that alone. As far as the other characters... there are a few who get fleshed out a little but you're constantly in motion with no time to really linger. There's no backtracking to previous areas once you clear an area (necessary for the plot to progress, sure) which makes the game feel pretty linear. It's much more in the style of an adventure game than an RPG, having no combat system and mostly being puzzle solving.
Where the game really shines is in the meta puzzles and storytelling, which are both done pretty well. Though it looks like the story isn't quite complete and won't be for about 18 days now, so we'll see if there's another ending coming out of that soon. The atmosphere is also great; both very serene courtesy of the music and ominous from the dark visual style. I think it works. Niko is a poor child in this scary world but everything is alright because you are there.
Honestly I just really like Niko as a character, both design-wise and personality-wise so I may be a little biased. But there's not much to complain about here; it's not too long but it feels as long as it needs to be at the very least. The puzzles are solid and not really moon logic-y at all. Maybe a bit too much having to close and relaunch the game though, hah.
Check it out if you're interested in a strongly narrative-based game, especially if you can get it on sale; I feel it's worth the full price & it's at least a little replayable as well, but I can see someone feeling a bit shorted at $10 for the length.

Trine 3 is a big step down from the first two Trine games. Frozenbyte hasn't done a very good translating the gameplay to a full 3D world as the game suffers from many of the same control and camera issues that plagued the early 3D platformers. Beautiful art and great soundtrack simply aren't enough to make up for the often frustrating gameplay.
Unfortunately, the game's issues are not restricted to poorly implemented 3D controls. Frozenbyte has admitted that they ran out of money during development and it shows. The game is rather short and the ending is very abrupt. The game ends on a massive cliffhanger and it's unclear if the story will ever be continued.
With all these faults I can't really recommend Trine 3 unless it's heavily discounted during a sale.
The good:
- Gorgeous art
- Nice soundtrack
- Some fun new puzzles
The bad:
- Short and unfinished story
- Poorly implemented 3D camera
- Imprecise 3D platforming
- No more difficulty levels and the game is extremely easy
- Skill tree has been removed
The ugly:
- Numerous minor graphics and physics glitches

This is pretty bad compared to the first 2 in the series, I would stay clear on the 3rd installment.
My Score - 5/10

The last level I beat took easily 50, if not 100, attempts. Which doesn't seem like a lot when you consider a level length is usually under 15 seconds. But the reverse of that means your 50 deaths are piling up every 5 seconds. It wears you down. It is satisfying to finally conquer a level though! The game is fair and when you get it right its because you darn well got it right. Luck isn't involved and I think that's important in a fair game of this ilk. Still, I got maybe a few more tries left in me but I just don't have that so-called "quick twitch shooter" capability in me to make it a feasible prospect to finish with my few shreds of remaining sanity intact. While I won't be likely to complete the game I certainly had fun getting to where I have. And, though against my normal personal review requirements, feel I got enough of what I wanted from the game to form an opinion worth sharing.
I got it in a bundle which was perfect. Its worth the price:time to check out bundled for sure. And to the speedrunning and quick twitch first-person shooter inclined player? It always saddens me when I have to write a negative critique about a GNU/Linux game (even if it's a proprietary one), but this game was very buggy and really left me with no choice... so here goes it.
The first problem I noticed was when tossing a grenade from behind cover. Although the line indicating where the grenade would be thrown looked fine, the grenades would always hit the cover you were behind and you would blow yourself up.
